support_parallel_printheads.label: Support parallel printheads
support_parallel_printheads.tooltip: Enable printer settings for machines that can use multiple printheads in parallel.

parallel_printheads_count.label: Parallel printheads count
parallel_printheads_count.tooltip: Set the number of parallel printheads for machines like OrangeStorm Giga printer.

parallel_printheads_bed_exclude_areas.label: Parallel printheads bed exclude areas
parallel_printheads_bed_exclude_areas.tooltip: Ordered list of bed exclude areas by parallel printhead count. Item 1 applies to one printhead, item 2 to two printheads, and so on. Leave an item empty for no excluded area.

bed_exclude_area.label: Excluded bed area
bed_exclude_area.tooltip: No-go zones on the build plate in XxY, XxY, ... polygon format (for example, the front-left filament cutter corner on X1 printers).

elefant_foot_compensation.label: Elephant foot compensation
elefant_foot_compensation.tooltip: This shrinks the first layer on the build plate to compensate for elephant foot effect.

elefant_foot_compensation_layers.label: Elephant foot compensation layers
elefant_foot_compensation_layers.tooltip: The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.

elefant_foot_layers_density.label: Elephant foot layers density
elefant_foot_layers_density.tooltip:
Density of internal solid infill for Elephant foot layers compensation.
The initial value for the second layer is set.
Subsequent layers become linearly denser by the height specified in elefant_foot_compensation_layers.

layer_height.label: Layer height
layer_height.tooltip: This is the height for each layer. Smaller layer heights give greater accuracy but longer printing time.

printable_height.label: Printable height
printable_height.tooltip: This is the maximum printable height which is limited by the height of the build area.

extruder_printable_height.label: Extruder printable height
extruder_printable_height.tooltip: Maximum printable height of this extruder which is limited by mechanism of printer.

preferred_orientation.label: Preferred orientation
preferred_orientation.tooltip: Automatically orient STL files on the Z axis upon initial import.

preset_names.label: Printer preset names
preset_names.tooltip: Names of presets related to the physical printer.

use_3mf.label: Use 3MF instead of G-code
use_3mf.tooltip: Enable this if the printer accepts a 3MF file as the print job. When enabled, Orca Slicer sends the sliced file as a .gcode.3mf, instead of a plain .gcode file.

flashforge_serial_number.label: Serial Number
flashforge_serial_number.tooltip: Flashforge local API requires the printer serial number.

reduce_crossing_wall.label: Avoid crossing walls
reduce_crossing_wall.tooltip: This detours to avoid traveling across walls, which may cause blobs on the surface.

max_travel_detour_distance.label: Avoid crossing walls - Max detour length
max_travel_detour_distance.tooltip: Maximum detour distance for avoiding crossing wall: The printer won't detour if the detour distance is larger than this value. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path. A value of 0 will disable this.

supertack_plate_temp.label: Other layers
supertack_plate_temp.tooltip: This is the bed temperature for layers except for the first one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate SuperTack.

cool_plate_temp.label: Other layers
cool_plate_temp.tooltip: This is the bed temperature for layers except for the first one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate.

textured_cool_plate_temp.label: Other layers
textured_cool_plate_temp.tooltip: This is the bed temperature for layers except for the first one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured Cool Plate.

eng_plate_temp.label: Other layers
eng_plate_temp.tooltip: This is the bed temperature for layers except for the first one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Engineering Plate.

hot_plate_temp.label: Other layers
hot_plate_temp.tooltip: This is the bed temperature for layers except for the first one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the High Temp Plate.

textured_plate_temp.label: Other layers
textured_plate_temp.tooltip: This is the bed temperature for layers except for the first one. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured PEI Plate.

supertack_plate_temp_initial_layer.label: First layer
supertack_plate_temp_initial_layer.tooltip: This is the bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate SuperTack.

cool_plate_temp_initial_layer.label: First layer
cool_plate_temp_initial_layer.tooltip: This is the bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Cool Plate.

textured_cool_plate_temp_initial_layer.label: First layer
textured_cool_plate_temp_initial_layer.tooltip: This is the bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured Cool Plate.

eng_plate_temp_initial_layer.label: First layer
eng_plate_temp_initial_layer.tooltip: This is the bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Engineering Plate.

hot_plate_temp_initial_layer.label: First layer
hot_plate_temp_initial_layer.tooltip: This is the bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the High Temp Plate.

textured_plate_temp_initial_layer.label: First layer
textured_plate_temp_initial_layer.tooltip: This is the bed temperature of the first layer. A value of 0 means the filament does not support printing on the Textured PEI Plate.

curr_bed_type.label: Bed type
curr_bed_type.tooltip: Plate types supported by the printer

default_bed_type.label: Default bed type
default_bed_type.tooltip: Default bed type for the printer (supports both numeric and string format).

other_layers_print_sequence_nums.label: The number of other layers print sequence

before_layer_change_gcode.label: Before layer change G-code
before_layer_change_gcode.tooltip: Custom G-code run at every layer change, right before the Z lift.

bottom_shell_layers.label: Bottom shell layers
bottom_shell_layers.tooltip: Number of solid bottom layers. If this comes out thinner than Bottom shell thickness, PancakeSlicer automatically adds layers to meet the minimum thickness.

bottom_shell_thickness.label: Minimum bottom thickness
bottom_shell_thickness.tooltip: Minimum thickness of the bottom solid shell, so thin layers still give a solid floor. 0 uses the layer count only.

gap_fill_target.label: Apply gap fill
gap_fill_target.tooltip:
Enables gap fill for the selected solid surfaces. The minimum gap length that will be filled can be controlled from the filter out tiny gaps option below.

Options:
1. Everywhere: Applies gap fill to top, bottom and internal solid surfaces for maximum strength
2. Top and Bottom surfaces: Applies gap fill to top and bottom surfaces only, balancing print speed, reducing potential over extrusion in the solid infill and making sure the top and bottom surfaces have no pinhole gaps
3. Nowhere: Disables gap fill for all solid infill areas

Note that if using the classic perimeter generator, gap fill may also be generated between perimeters, if a full width line cannot fit between them. That perimeter gap fill is not controlled by this setting.

If you would like all gap fill, including the classic perimeter generated one, removed, set the filter out tiny gaps value to a large number, like 999999.

However this is not advised, as gap fill between perimeters is contributing to the model's strength. For models where excessive gap fill is generated between perimeters, a better option would be to switch to the arachne wall generator and use this option to control whether the cosmetic top and bottom surface gap fill is generated.

enable_overhang_bridge_fan.label: Force cooling for overhangs and bridges
enable_overhang_bridge_fan.tooltip: Enable this option to allow adjustment of the part cooling fan speed for specifically for overhangs, internal and external bridges. Setting the fan speed specifically for these features can improve overall print quality and reduce warping.

overhang_fan_speed.label: Overhangs and external bridges fan speed
overhang_fan_speed.tooltip:
Use this part cooling fan speed when printing bridges or overhang walls with an overhang threshold that exceeds the value set in the 'Overhangs cooling threshold' parameter above. Increasing the cooling specifically for overhangs and bridges can improve the overall print quality of these features.

Please note, this fan speed is clamped on the lower end by the minimum fan speed threshold set above. It is also adjusted upwards up to the maximum fan speed threshold when the minimum layer time threshold is not met.

overhang_fan_threshold.label: Overhang cooling activation threshold
overhang_fan_threshold.tooltip: When the overhang exceeds this specified threshold, force the cooling fan to run at the 'Overhang Fan Speed' set below. This threshold is expressed as a percentage, indicating the portion of each line's width that is unsupported by the layer beneath it. Setting this value to 0% forces the cooling fan to run for all outer walls, regardless of the overhang degree.

bridge_angle.label: External bridge angle
bridge_angle.tooltip: Fixed angle for external bridges. Leave at 0° to automatically bridge across the shortest span, or use 180° to force a 0° horizontal bridge.

internal_bridge_angle.label: Internal bridge infill direction
internal_bridge_angle.tooltip:
Internal Bridging angle override.
If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically for each specific bridge.
Otherwise the provided angle will be used according to:
 - The absolute coordinates
 - The absolute coordinates + Model rotation: If Align directions to model is enabled
 - The optimal automatic angle + this value: If 'Relative Bridge Angle' is enabled

Use 180° for zero absolute angle.

relative_bridge_angle.label: Relative bridge angle
relative_bridge_angle.tooltip: When enabled, the bridge angle values are added to the automatically calculated bridge direction instead of overriding it.

bridge_density.label: External bridge density
bridge_density.tooltip: Spacing density of external bridge lines. 100% is a solid bridge; lower values space the lines out.

internal_bridge_density.label: Internal bridge density
internal_bridge_density.tooltip:
Controls the density (spacing) of internal bridge lines.
Internal bridges act as intermediate support between sparse infill and top solid infill and can strongly affect top surface quality.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):
  - Pros: Improves internal bridge strength and support under top layers, reducing sagging and improving top-surface finish.
  - Cons: Increases material use and print time; excessive density may cause overextrusion and internal stresses.

- Lower than 100% density (Min 10%):
  - Pros: Can reduce pillowing and improve cooling (more airflow through the bridge), and may speed up printing.
  - Cons: May reduce internal support, increasing the risk of sagging and top surface defects.

This option works particularly well when combined with the second internal bridge over infill option to improve bridging further before solid infill is extruded.

bridge_flow.label: Bridge flow ratio
bridge_flow.tooltip:
This value governs the thickness of the external (visible) bridge layer.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This can improve line contact and strength.
Values below 1.0: Reduce the amount of material while adjusting line spacing to maintain contact. This can improve sagging.

The actual bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

bridge_line_width.label: Bridge
bridge_line_width.tooltip:
Line width of the Bridge. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
Recommended to use with a higher Bridge density or Bridge flow ratio.

The maximum value is 100% or the nozzle diameter.
If set to 0, the line width will match the Internal solid infill width.

internal_bridge_flow.label: Internal bridge flow ratio
internal_bridge_flow.tooltip:
This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill so increasing it may increase strength and upper layer quality.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This can improve line contact and strength.
Values below 1.0: Reduce the amount of material while adjusting line spacing to maintain contact. This can improve sagging.

The actual bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

top_solid_infill_flow_ratio.label: Top surface flow ratio
top_solid_infill_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for top solid infill. You can decrease it slightly to have smooth surface finish.

The actual top surface flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio.label: Bottom surface flow ratio
bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio.tooltip: Flow multiplier for bottom solid layers (multiplied with your filament and object flow ratios).

set_other_flow_ratios.label: Set other flow ratios
set_other_flow_ratios.tooltip: Change flow ratios for other extrusion path types.

first_layer_flow_ratio.label: First layer flow ratio
first_layer_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material on the first layer for the extrusion path roles listed in this section.

For the first layer, the actual flow ratio for each path role (does not affect brims and skirts) will be multiplied by this value.

outer_wall_flow_ratio.label: Outer wall flow ratio
outer_wall_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for outer walls.

The actual outer wall flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

inner_wall_flow_ratio.label: Inner wall flow ratio
inner_wall_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for inner walls.

The actual inner wall flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

overhang_flow_ratio.label: Overhang flow ratio
overhang_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for overhangs.

The actual overhang flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

sparse_infill_flow_ratio.label: Sparse infill flow ratio
sparse_infill_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for sparse infill.

The actual sparse infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

internal_solid_infill_flow_ratio.label: Internal solid infill flow ratio
internal_solid_infill_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for internal solid infill.

The actual internal solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

gap_fill_flow_ratio.label: Gap fill flow ratio
gap_fill_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for filling the gaps.

The actual gap filling flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

support_flow_ratio.label: Support flow ratio
support_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for support.

The actual support flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

support_interface_flow_ratio.label: Support interface flow ratio
support_interface_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for the support interface.

The actual support interface flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

precise_outer_wall.label: Precise wall
precise_outer_wall.tooltip: Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency. NOTE: This option will be ignored for outer-inner or inner-outer-inner wall sequences.

only_one_wall_top.label: Only one wall on top surfaces
only_one_wall_top.tooltip: Use only one wall on flat top surfaces, to give more space to the top infill pattern.

min_width_top_surface.label: One wall threshold
min_width_top_surface.tooltip:
If a top surface has to be printed and it's partially covered by another layer, it won't be considered at a top layer where its width is below this value. This can be useful to not let the 'one perimeter on top' trigger on surface that should be covered only by perimeters. This value can be a mm or a % of the perimeter extrusion width.
Warning: If enabled, artifacts can be created if you have some thin features on the next layer, like letters. Set this setting to 0 to remove these artifacts.

only_one_wall_first_layer.label: Only one wall on first layer
only_one_wall_first_layer.tooltip: Use only one wall on first layer, to give more space to the bottom infill pattern.

extra_perimeters_on_overhangs.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs
extra_perimeters_on_overhangs.tooltip: Create additional perimeter paths over steep overhangs and areas where bridges cannot be anchored.

overhang_reverse.label: Reverse on even
overhang_reverse.tooltip:
Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on even layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs.

This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part walls.

overhang_reverse_internal_only.label: Reverse only internal perimeters
overhang_reverse_internal_only.tooltip:
Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters.

This setting greatly reduces part stresses as they are now distributed in alternating directions. This should reduce part warping while also maintaining external wall quality. This feature can be very useful for warp prone material, like ABS/ASA, and also for elastic filaments, like TPU and Silk PLA. It can also help reduce warping on floating regions over supports.

For this setting to be the most effective, it is recommended to set the Reverse Threshold to 0 so that all internal walls print in alternating directions on even layers irrespective of their overhang degree.

counterbore_hole_bridging.label: Bridge counterbore holes
counterbore_hole_bridging.tooltip:
This option creates bridges for counterbore holes, allowing them to be printed without support. Available modes include:
1. None: No bridge is created
2. Partially Bridged: Only a part of the unsupported area will be bridged
3. Sacrificial Layer: A full sacrificial bridge layer is created

overhang_reverse_threshold.label: Reverse threshold
overhang_reverse_threshold.tooltip:
Number of mm the overhang need to be for the reversal to be considered useful. Can be a % of the perimeter width.
Value 0 enables reversal on every even layers regardless.
When Detect overhang wall is not enabled, this option is ignored and reversal happens on every even layers regardless.

enable_overhang_speed.label: Slow down for overhangs
enable_overhang_speed.tooltip: Enable this option to slow down when printing overhangs. The speeds for different overhang percentages are set below.

slowdown_for_curled_perimeters.label: Slow down for curled perimeters
slowdown_for_curled_perimeters.tooltip:
Enable this option to slow down printing in areas where perimeters may have curled upwards.
For example, additional slowdown will be applied when printing overhangs on sharp corners like the front of the Benchy hull, reducing curling which compounds over multiple layers.

It is generally recommended to have this option switched on unless your printer cooling is powerful enough or the print speed is slow enough that perimeter curling does not happen. 
If printing with a high external perimeter speed, this parameter may introduce wall artifacts when slowing down, due to the potentially large variance in print speeds causing the extruder to be unable to keep up with the requested flow change.
Root cause of these artifacts is most likely PA tuning being slightly off, especially when combined with a high PA smooth time.

Recommendations when enabling this option:
1. Reduce Pressure Advance smooth time to 0.015 - 0.02 so the extruder reacts quickly to the speed changes.
2. Increase the minimum print speeds to limit the magnitude of the slowdown and reduce the variance between fast and slow segments.
3. If artifacts still appear, enable Extrusion Rate Smoothing (ERS) to further smooth the flow transitions.

Note: When this option is enabled, overhang perimeters are treated like overhangs, meaning the overhang speed is applied even if the overhanging perimeter is part of a bridge.
For example, when the perimeters are 100% overhanging, with no wall supporting them from underneath, the 100% overhang speed will be applied.

bridge_speed.label: External
bridge_speed.tooltip:
Speed of the externally visible bridge extrusions.

In addition, if Slow down for curled perimeters is disabled or Classic overhang mode is enabled, it will be the print speed of overhang walls that are supported by less than 13%, whether they are part of a bridge or an overhang.

internal_bridge_speed.label: Internal
internal_bridge_speed.tooltip: Speed of internal bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.

brim_width.label: Brim width
brim_width.tooltip: This is the distance from the model to the outermost brim line.

leading_brim_length.label: Leading brim length
leading_brim_length.tooltip:
Belt printers only. Extends the brim AHEAD of the object along the belt, on every downhill-facing edge of its contact area - both the object's first contact with the belt and any island that lands later. This apron is laid onto the belt before the object reaches it, so the leading edge has something already stuck down to hold on to.

Measured on the belt surface, and added on top of Brim width: the brim reaches Brim-object gap + Leading brim length + Brim width ahead of the object. Set Brim-object gap to 0, or the apron will not touch the object it is meant to anchor.

On a tilted belt each layer lays one strip of the brim, so the thickness of the resulting brim sheet is set by flow rather than by layer height. Use Brim flow ratio to tune it.

Set to 0 to disable.

extra_brim_width.label: Extra brim width
extra_brim_width.tooltip:
Belt printers only. Widens the brim SIDEWAYS, across the belt, without extending it further ahead of or behind the object. Use it when a part needs more grip along its length than Brim width alone gives.

Measured on the belt surface, and added on top of Brim width: the brim reaches Brim-object gap + Brim width + Extra brim width to either side of the object. To extend the brim ahead of the object instead, use Leading brim length.

Set to 0 to disable.

brim_type.label: Brim type
brim_type.tooltip: This controls the generation of the brim at outer and/or inner side of models. Auto means the brim width is analyzed and calculated automatically.

brim_object_gap.label: Brim-object gap
brim_object_gap.tooltip: This creates a gap between the innermost brim line and the object and can make the brim easier to remove.

brim_flow_ratio.label: Brim flow ratio
brim_flow_ratio.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for brims.

The actual brim flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

Note: The resulting value will not be affected by the first-layer flow ratio.

brim_use_efc_outline.label: Brim follows compensated outline
brim_use_efc_outline.tooltip:
When enabled, the brim is aligned with the first-layer perimeter geometry after Elephant Foot Compensation is applied.
This option is intended for cases where Elephant Foot Compensation significantly alters the first-layer footprint.

If your current setup already works well, enabling it may be unnecessary and can cause the brim to fuse with upper layers.

combine_brims.label: Combine brims
combine_brims.tooltip: Combine multiple brims into one when they are close to each other. This can improve brim adhesion.

brim_ears.label: Brim ears
brim_ears.tooltip: Only draw brim over the sharp edges of the model.

brim_ears_max_angle.label: Brim ear max angle
brim_ears_max_angle.tooltip:
Maximum angle to let a brim ear appear.
If set to 0, no brim will be created.
If set to ~180, brim will be created on everything but straight sections.

brim_ears_detection_length.label: Brim ear detection radius
brim_ears_detection_length.tooltip:
The geometry will be decimated before detecting sharp angles. This parameter indicates the minimum length of the deviation for the decimation.
0 to deactivate.

brim_ears_outer_only.label: Brim ears outer only
brim_ears_outer_only.tooltip: Generate mouse ears only on the outer contour of the model, excluding holes and enclosed sections.

compatible_printers_condition.label: Condition
compatible_printers_condition.tooltip: A Boolean expression using the configuration values of an active printer profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active printer profile.

compatible_prints_condition.label: Condition
compatible_prints_condition.tooltip: A Boolean expression using the configuration values of an active print profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active print profile.

print_sequence.label: Print sequence
print_sequence.tooltip: This determines the print sequence, allowing you to print layer-by-layer or object-by-object.

print_order.label: Intra-layer order
print_order.tooltip:
Order in which object instances are visited within a single layer, which controls how much travel is spent moving between them.

Default: nearest-neighbor chaining, refined with 2-opt and crossing removal. A good general choice.
As object list: instances are printed in the same order as the object list, without any path optimization. Use it when you need a predictable, manually controlled order.
Best of all (shortest path): every strategy is evaluated and the shortest one is used. The object instance order is decided once for the whole print, while the ordering of individual islands is decided per layer, so different layers may end up using different strategies. Slightly slower to slice.
Snake: serpentine row-by-row traversal, refined with 2-opt. Well suited to regular grids of many small parts.

With multiple filaments or tools in the same layer, minimizing tool changes takes priority: objects are grouped by filament first and this setting only orders the instances within each filament group, so the overall sequence may not look like the shortest path across the plate.

slow_down_for_layer_cooling.label: Slow printing down for better layer cooling
slow_down_for_layer_cooling.tooltip: Enable this option to slow printing speed down to ensure that the final layer time is not shorter than the layer time threshold in "Max fan speed threshold", so that the layer can be cooled for a longer time. This can improve the quality for small details.

default_acceleration.label: Normal printing
default_acceleration.tooltip: This is the default acceleration for both normal printing and travel after the first layer.

initial_layer_travel_acceleration.label: First layer travel
initial_layer_travel_acceleration.tooltip:
Travel acceleration of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Acceleration.

bridge_acceleration.label: Bridge acceleration
bridge_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration used while bridging (% values scale from outer wall acceleration).

default_filament_profile.label: Default filament profile
default_filament_profile.tooltip: Default filament profile when switching to this machine profile.

default_print_profile.label: Default process profile
default_print_profile.tooltip: Default process profile when switching to this machine profile.

activate_air_filtration.label: Air filtration
activate_air_filtration.tooltip: Turns on the chamber exhaust/filtration fan (M106 P3 S0-255).

activate_air_filtration_during_print.tooltip: Overrides any filtration fan speed set in custom G-code while printing.

activate_air_filtration_on_completion.tooltip: Overrides any filtration fan speed set in custom G-code once the print is done.

during_print_exhaust_fan_speed.label: Fan speed
during_print_exhaust_fan_speed.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan during printing. This speed will override the speed in filament custom G-code.

complete_print_exhaust_fan_speed.label: Fan speed
complete_print_exhaust_fan_speed.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan after printing completes.

close_fan_the_first_x_layers.label: No cooling for the first
close_fan_the_first_x_layers.tooltip: Turn off all cooling fans for the first few layers. This can be used to improve build plate adhesion.

bridge_no_support.label: Don't support bridges
bridge_no_support.tooltip: This disables supporting bridges, which decreases the amount of support required. Bridges can usually be printed directly without support over a reasonable distance.

thick_bridges.label: Thick external bridges
thick_bridges.tooltip:
If enabled, bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases bridge strength and reliability, allowing longer spans, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, bridges may look better but are generally reliable only for shorter spans.

thick_internal_bridges.label: Thick internal bridges
thick_internal_bridges.tooltip:
If enabled, internal bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases internal bridge strength and reliability when printed over sparse infill, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, internal bridges may look better but can be less reliable over sparse infill.

enable_extra_bridge_layer.label: Extra bridge layers (beta)
enable_extra_bridge_layer.tooltip:
This option enables the generation of an extra bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges.

Extra bridge layers help improve bridge appearance and reliability, as the solid infill is better supported. This is especially useful in fast printers, where the bridge and solid infill speeds vary greatly. The extra bridge layer results in reduced pillowing on top surfaces, as well as reduced separation of the external bridge layer from its surrounding perimeters.

It is generally recommended to set this to at least 'External bridge only', unless specific issues with the sliced model are found.

Options:
1. Disabled - does not generate second bridge layers. This is the default and is set for compatibility purposes
2. External bridge only - generates second bridge layers for external-facing bridges only. Please note that small bridges that are shorter or narrower than the set number of perimeters will be skipped as they would not benefit from a second bridge layer. If generated, the second bridge layer will be extruded parallel to the first bridge layer to reinforce the bridge strength
3. Internal bridge only - generates second bridge layers for internal bridges over sparse infill only. Please note that the internal bridges count towards the top shell layer count of your model. The second internal bridge layer will be extruded as close to perpendicular to the first as possible. If multiple regions in the same island, with varying bridge angles are present, the last region of that island will be selected as the angle reference
4. Apply to all - generates second bridge layers for both internal and external-facing bridges

dont_filter_internal_bridges.label: Filter out small internal bridges
dont_filter_internal_bridges.tooltip:
This option can help reduce pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.
By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding up printing without too much compromise on top surface quality.
However, in heavily slanted or curved models, especially where too low a sparse infill density is used, this may result in curling of the unsupported solid infill, causing pillowing.
Enabling limited filtering or no filtering will print internal bridge layer over slightly unsupported internal solid infill. The options below control the sensitivity of the filtering, i.e. they control where internal bridges are created:
1. Filter - enables this option. This is the default behavior and works well in most cases
2. Limited filtering - creates internal bridges on heavily slanted surfaces while avoiding unnecessary bridges. This works well for most difficult models
3. No filtering - creates internal bridges on every potential internal overhang. This option is useful for heavily slanted top surface models; however, in most cases, it creates too many unnecessary bridges.

max_bridge_length.label: Max bridge length
max_bridge_length.tooltip: This is the maximum length of bridges that don't need support. Set it to 0 if you want all bridges to be supported, and set it to a very large value if you don't want any bridges to be supported.

machine_end_gcode.label: End G-code
machine_end_gcode.tooltip: Add end G-Code when finishing the entire print.
machine_end_gcode.default:
M104 S0 ; turn off temperature
G28 X0  ; home X axis
M84     ; disable motors

printing_by_object_gcode.label: Between Object G-code
printing_by_object_gcode.tooltip: Insert G-code between objects. This parameter will only come into effect when you print your models object by object.

filament_end_gcode.label: End G-code
filament_end_gcode.tooltip: Add end G-code when finishing the printing of this filament.

ensure_vertical_shell_thickness.label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
ensure_vertical_shell_thickness.tooltip:
Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers)
None: No solid infill will be added anywhere. Caution: Use this option carefully if your model has sloped surfaces
Critical Only: Avoid adding solid infill for walls
Moderate: Add solid infill for heavily sloping surfaces only
All: Add solid infill for all suitable sloping surfaces
Default value is All.

top_surface_pattern.label: Top surface pattern
top_surface_pattern.tooltip: This is the line pattern for top surface infill.

top_surface_density.label: Top surface density
top_surface_density.tooltip: Density of top surface layer. A value of 100% creates a fully solid, smooth top layer. Reducing this value results in a textured top surface, according to the chosen top surface pattern. A value of 0% will result in only the walls on the top layer being created. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.

top_surface_expansion.label: Top surface expansion
top_surface_expansion.tooltip:
Expands the top surfaces by this distance to connect distinct top surfaces and fill gaps.
Useful for cases where the top surface is interrupted by a raised feature, such as text on a plane. Expanding it removes the holes beneath these features and creates a continuous path with a better finish for printing on top. The expansion is applied to the original top surface, before any other processing such as bridging or overhang detection.

top_surface_expansion_margin.label: Top expansion wall margin
top_surface_expansion_margin.tooltip:
Using “Top surface expansion” may cause a surface that did not previously touch the model's outer walls to now do so.
This can cause contraction marks (such as the hull line) on the outer walls.
By adding a small margin, this contraction will not occur directly on the walls, thereby preventing a visible mark.

top_surface_expansion_direction.label: Top expansion direction
top_surface_expansion_direction.tooltip:
Direction in which the top surface expansion grows.
 - Inward grows into the holes and gaps left by features rising from the middle of a top surface.
 - Outward grows the outer edge of the surface, connecting surfaces separated by features that can divide a surface, such as a lattice pattern.
 - Inward and Outward does both.

bottom_surface_pattern.label: Bottom surface pattern
bottom_surface_pattern.tooltip: Toolpath pattern used for the bottom surface (excluding bridges).

bottom_surface_density.label: Bottom surface density
bottom_surface_density.tooltip: Line density of the first bottom layer. For visual textures, not to correct over-extrusion. Lower values reduce bed grip.

top_surface_fill_order.label: Top surface fill order
top_surface_fill_order.tooltip:
Direction in which top surfaces are filled when using a center-based pattern (Concentric, Spiral Inset, Archimedean Chords, Octagram Spiral).
Outward starts at the center of the surface, so any excess material is pushed towards the edge where it is least visible. Inward starts at the edge and ends with the tight curves at the center.
Default uses shortest-path ordering, which may run in either direction.

bottom_surface_fill_order.label: Bottom surface fill direction
bottom_surface_fill_order.tooltip: Fill direction for center-based bottom patterns (Concentric, Spiral Inset, Archimedean Chords, Octagram Spiral). Inward prints the outer loops first, so small center rings do not peel up on the first layer. Outward starts in the middle and pushes excess plastic outward.

internal_solid_infill_pattern.label: Internal solid infill pattern
internal_solid_infill_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.

outer_wall_line_width.label: Outer wall
outer_wall_line_width.tooltip: Line width of outer wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

outer_wall_speed.label: Outer wall
outer_wall_speed.tooltip: This is the printing speed for the outer walls of parts. These are generally printed slower than inner walls for higher quality.

small_perimeter_speed.label: Small perimeters
small_perimeter_speed.tooltip: This separate setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= small_perimeter_threshold (usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the outer wall speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

small_perimeter_threshold.label: Small perimeters threshold
small_perimeter_threshold.tooltip: This sets the threshold for small perimeter length. Default threshold is 0mm.

small_support_perimeter_speed.label: Small support perimeters
small_support_perimeter_speed.tooltip: Same as "Small perimeters", but for supports. This separate setting will affect the speed of support for areas <= `small_support_perimeter_threshold`. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%), it will be calculated on the support or support interface speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

small_support_perimeter_threshold.label: Small support perimeters threshold
small_support_perimeter_threshold.tooltip: This sets the threshold for small support perimeter length. The default threshold is 0mm.

wall_sequence.label: Walls printing order
wall_sequence.tooltip:
Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls.

Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighbouring perimeter while printing. However, this option results in slightly reduced surface quality as the external perimeter is deformed by being squashed to the internal perimeter.

Use Inner/Outer/Inner for the best external surface finish and dimensional accuracy as the external wall is printed undisturbed from an internal perimeter. However, overhang performance will reduce as there is no internal perimeter to print the external wall against. This option requires a minimum of 3 walls to be effective as it prints the internal walls from the 3rd perimeter onwards first, then the external perimeter and, finally, the first internal perimeter. This option is recommended against the Outer/Inner option in most cases.

Use Outer/Inner for the same external wall quality and dimensional accuracy benefits of Inner/Outer/Inner option. However, the Z seams will appear less consistent as the first extrusion of a new layer starts on a visible surface.

is_infill_first.label: Print infill first
is_infill_first.tooltip:
Order of wall/infill. When the tickbox is unchecked the walls are printed first, which works best in most cases.

Printing infill first may help with extreme overhangs as the walls have the neighbouring infill to adhere to. However, the infill will slightly push out the printed walls where it is attached to them, resulting in a worse external surface finish. It can also cause the infill to shine through the external surfaces of the part.

wall_direction.label: Wall loop direction
wall_direction.tooltip:
The direction which the contour wall loops are extruded when looking down from the top.
Holes are printed in the opposite direction to the contour to maintain alignment with layers whose contour polygons are incomplete and change direction, also partially forming the contour of a hole.

This option will be disabled if spiral vase mode is enabled.

extruder_clearance_dist_to_rod.label: Distance to rod
extruder_clearance_dist_to_rod.tooltip: Horizontal distance of the nozzle tip to the rod's farther edge. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

extruder_clearance_height_to_rod.label: Height to rod
extruder_clearance_height_to_rod.tooltip: Distance from the nozzle tip to the lower rod. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

extruder_clearance_height_to_lid.label: Height to lid
extruder_clearance_height_to_lid.tooltip: Distance from the nozzle tip to the lid. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

extruder_clearance_radius.label: Radius
extruder_clearance_radius.tooltip: Clearance radius around extruder: used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

bed_mesh_min.label: Bed mesh min point
bed_mesh_min.tooltip: Minimum XY coordinates the bed probe can safely reach. Default (-99999, -99999) leaves the whole bed open.

bed_mesh_max.label: Bed mesh max point
bed_mesh_max.tooltip: Furthest XY coordinates the bed probe can safely reach without the probe offset pushing the toolhead out of bounds. Default (99999, 99999) leaves the whole bed open.

bed_mesh_probe_distance.label: Probe grid spacing
bed_mesh_probe_distance.tooltip: Target X/Y spacing between bed mesh probe points (50 mm by default).

adaptive_bed_mesh_margin.label: Mesh margin
adaptive_bed_mesh_margin.tooltip: Extra padding around the print area (in X and Y) when probing an adaptive bed mesh.

extruder_colour.label: Extruder Color
extruder_colour.tooltip: Only used as a visual help on UI.

filament_flow_ratio.label: Flow ratio
filament_flow_ratio.tooltip: The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow.

print_flow_ratio.label: Flow ratio
print_flow_ratio.tooltip:
The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow.

The final object flow ratio is this value multiplied by the filament flow ratio.

enable_pressure_advance.label: Enable pressure advance
enable_pressure_advance.tooltip: Enable pressure advance, auto calibration result will be overwritten once enabled.

pressure_advance.label: Pressure advance
pressure_advance.tooltip: Pressure advance (Klipper) AKA Linear advance factor (Marlin).

adaptive_pressure_advance.label: Adaptive pressure advance (beta)
adaptive_pressure_advance.tooltip: The best Pressure Advance (PA) usually falls as speed and acceleration rise, so one fixed PA trades bulging slow corners against thin fast moves. Adaptive PA sets PA from the measured flow and acceleration while printing. The PA value above remains the fallback and the value at tool changes.

adaptive_pressure_advance_model.label: Adaptive PA measurements (beta)
adaptive_pressure_advance_model.tooltip:
Calibrated PA, volumetric flow and acceleration triplets, one per line, separated by commas. For example:
0.04,3.96,3000
0.033,3.96,10000
0.029,7.91,3000
0.026,7.91,10000

How to calibrate:
1. Run the PA test at 3 or more speeds (outer wall, inner wall and the fastest infill), at the lowest and highest print accelerations, up to the input shaper's maximum.
2. Note the best PA for each flow and acceleration. Set the preview color scheme to Flow to read the mm³/s value. The best PA should fall as flow rises.
3. Enter the triplets here and save the filament profile.

adaptive_pressure_advance_overhangs.label: Adaptive PA inside features (beta)
adaptive_pressure_advance_overhangs.tooltip: Changes Pressure Advance within a feature when its flow changes, as on variable-width corners and overhangs. Experimental: calibrate the PA model first. Not for Prusa firmware, which pauses briefly on each PA change and leaves blobs.

adaptive_pressure_advance_bridges.label: Bridge pressure advance
adaptive_pressure_advance_bridges.tooltip: Pressure Advance while bridging. 0 uses the wall PA. Nozzle pressure drops over air, so a slightly lower PA on bridges prevents under-extrusion where the bridge lands on the part.

line_width.label: Default
line_width.tooltip: Default line width if other line widths are set to 0. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

reduce_fan_stop_start_freq.label: Keep fan always on
reduce_fan_stop_start_freq.tooltip: Enabling this setting means that part cooling fan will never stop entirely and will instead run at least at minimum speed to reduce the frequency of starting and stopping.

dont_slow_down_outer_wall.label: Don't slow down outer walls
dont_slow_down_outer_wall.tooltip:
If enabled, this setting will ensure external perimeters are not slowed down to meet the minimum layer time. This is particularly helpful in the below scenarios:
1. To avoid changes in shine when printing glossy filaments
2. To avoid changes in external wall speed which may create slight wall artifacts that appear like Z banding
3. To avoid printing at speeds which cause VFAs (fine artifacts) on the external walls

fan_cooling_layer_time.label: Layer time
fan_cooling_layer_time.tooltip: The part cooling fan will be enabled for layers where the estimated time is shorter than this value. Fan speed is interpolated between the minimum and maximum fan speeds according to layer printing time.

default_filament_colour.label: Default color
default_filament_colour.tooltip:
Default filament color.
Right click to reset value to system default.

filament_colour.label: Color
filament_colour.tooltip: Only used as a visual help on UI.

filament_notes.label: Filament notes
filament_notes.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the filament here.

required_nozzle_HRC.label: Required nozzle HRC
required_nozzle_HRC.tooltip: Minimum HRC of nozzle required to print the filament. A value of 0 means no checking of the nozzle's HRC.

filament_map_2.label: Filament map plus for multi nozzle
filament_map_2.tooltip: Filament map to the index identified by extruder and nozzle_volume_type

physical_extruder_map.label: Map the logical extruder to physical extruder
physical_extruder_map.tooltip: Map the logical extruder to physical extruder.

filament_map_mode.label: filament mapping mode
filament_map_mode.tooltip: Filament mapping mode used as plate param.

filament_flush_temp.label: Flush temperature
filament_flush_temp.tooltip: Temperature when flushing filament. 0 indicates the upper bound of the recommended nozzle temperature range.

filament_flush_temp_fast.label: Flush temperature
filament_flush_temp_fast.tooltip: Flush temperature used in fast purge mode.

filament_flush_volumetric_speed.label: Flush volumetric speed
filament_flush_volumetric_speed.tooltip: Volumetric speed when flushing filament. 0 indicates the max volumetric speed.

filament_max_volumetric_speed.label: Max volumetric speed
filament_max_volumetric_speed.tooltip: This setting is the volume of filament that can be melted and extruded per second. Printing speed is limited by max volumetric speed, in case of too high and unreasonable speed setting. This value cannot be zero.

machine_load_filament_time.label: Filament load time
machine_load_filament_time.tooltip: Time to load new filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

machine_unload_filament_time.label: Filament unload time
machine_unload_filament_time.tooltip: Time to unload old filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

machine_tool_change_time.label: Tool change time
machine_tool_change_time.tooltip: Time taken to switch tools. It's usually applicable for tool changers or multi-tool machines. For single-extruder multi-material machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

bed_temperature_formula.label: Multi-filament bed temp rule
bed_temperature_formula.tooltip: Sets whether the heated bed uses the first filament's temperature or the highest temperature among all filaments on the plate.

filament_diameter.label: Diameter
filament_diameter.tooltip: Filament diameter is used to calculate extrusion variables in G-code, so it is important that this is accurate and precise.

pellet_flow_coefficient.label: Pellet flow coefficient
pellet_flow_coefficient.tooltip:
Pellet flow coefficient is empirically derived and allows for volume calculation for pellet printers.

Internally it is converted to filament_diameter. All other volume calculations remain the same.

filament_diameter = sqrt( (4 * pellet_flow_coefficient) / PI )

filament_adaptive_volumetric_speed.label: Adaptive volumetric speed
filament_adaptive_volumetric_speed.tooltip:
When enabled, the extrusion flow is limited by the smaller of the fitted value (calculated from line width and layer height) and the user-defined maximum flow. When disabled, only the user-defined maximum flow is applied.

Note: Experimental and incomplete feature imported from BBS. Functional for some profiles that already have the variable saved.

filament_shrink.label: Shrinkage (XY)
filament_shrink.tooltip:
Enter the shrinkage percentage that the filament will get after cooling (94% if you measure 94mm instead of 100mm). The part will be scaled in XY to compensate. For multi-material prints, ensure filament shrinkage matches across all used filaments
Be sure to allow enough space between objects, as this compensation is done after the checks.

filament_shrinkage_compensation_z.label: Shrinkage (Z)
filament_shrinkage_compensation_z.tooltip: Enter the shrinkage percentage that the filament will get after cooling (94% if you measure 94mm instead of 100mm). The part will be scaled in Z to compensate.

filament_loading_speed.label: Loading speed
filament_loading_speed.tooltip: Speed used for loading the filament on the wipe tower.

filament_loading_speed_start.label: Loading speed at the start
filament_loading_speed_start.tooltip: Speed used at the very beginning of loading phase.

filament_unloading_speed.label: Unloading speed
filament_unloading_speed.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the filament on the wipe tower (does not affect initial part of unloading just after ramming).

filament_unloading_speed_start.label: Unloading speed at the start
filament_unloading_speed_start.tooltip: Speed used for unloading the tip of the filament immediately after ramming.

filament_toolchange_delay.label: Delay after unloading
filament_toolchange_delay.tooltip: Time to wait after the filament is unloaded. May help to get reliable tool changes with flexible materials that may need more time to shrink to original dimensions.

filament_cooling_moves.label: Number of cooling moves
filament_cooling_moves.tooltip: Filament is cooled by being moved back and forth in the cooling tubes. Specify desired number of these moves.

filament_stamping_distance.label: Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube
filament_stamping_distance.tooltip: If set to non-zero value, filament is moved toward the nozzle between the individual cooling moves ("stamping"). This option configures how long this movement should be before the filament is retracted again.

filament_cooling_initial_speed.label: Speed of the first cooling move
filament_cooling_initial_speed.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating beginning at this speed.

filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower.label: Minimal purge on wipe tower
filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower.tooltip: After a tool change, the exact position of the newly loaded filament inside the nozzle may not be known, and the filament pressure is likely not yet stable. Before purging the print head into an infill or a sacrificial object, Orca Slicer will always prime this amount of material into the wipe tower to produce successive infill or sacrificial object extrusions reliably.

filament_cooling_before_tower.label: Wipe tower cooling
filament_cooling_before_tower.tooltip: Temperature drop before entering filament tower

filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_d.label: Interface layer pre-extrusion distance
filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_d.tooltip: Pre-extrusion distance for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_l.label: Interface layer pre-extrusion length
filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_l.tooltip: Pre-extrusion length for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

filament_tower_ironing_area.label: Tower ironing area
filament_tower_ironing_area.tooltip: Ironing area for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

filament_tower_interface_purge_volume.label: Interface layer purge length
filament_tower_interface_purge_volume.tooltip: Purge length for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

filament_tower_interface_print_temp.label: Interface layer print temperature
filament_tower_interface_print_temp.tooltip: Print temperature for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet). If set to -1, use max recommended nozzle temperature.

filament_cooling_final_speed.label: Speed of the last cooling move
filament_cooling_final_speed.tooltip: Cooling moves are gradually accelerating towards this speed.

filament_ramming_parameters.label: Ramming parameters
filament_ramming_parameters.tooltip: This string is edited by RammingDialog and contains ramming specific parameters.

filament_multitool_ramming.label: Enable ramming for multi-tool setups
filament_multitool_ramming.tooltip: Perform ramming when using multi-tool printer (i.e. when the 'Single Extruder Multimaterial' in Printer Settings is unchecked). When checked, a small amount of filament is rapidly extruded on the wipe tower just before the tool change. This option is only used when the wipe tower is enabled.

filament_multitool_ramming_volume.label: Multi-tool ramming volume
filament_multitool_ramming_volume.tooltip: The volume to be rammed before the tool change.

filament_multitool_ramming_flow.label: Multi-tool ramming flow
filament_multitool_ramming_flow.tooltip: Flow used for ramming the filament before the tool change.

filament_density.label: Density
filament_density.tooltip: Filament density, for statistical purposes only.

filament_soluble.label: Soluble material
filament_soluble.tooltip: Soluble material is commonly used to print supports and support interfaces.

filament_change_length.label: Filament ramming length
filament_change_length.tooltip: When changing the extruder, it is recommended to extrude a certain length of filament from the original extruder. This helps minimize nozzle oozing.

filament_is_support.label: Support material
filament_is_support.tooltip: Support material is commonly used to print supports and support interfaces.

filament_is_mixed.label: Is mixed filament
filament_is_mixed.tooltip: Whether this filament slot is a mixed filament composed of multiple physical filaments

filament_mixed_components.label: Mixed filament components
filament_mixed_components.tooltip: Comma-separated 1-based indices of component filaments, e.g. "1,3"

filament_mixed_sublayer_ratios.label: Mixed filament sublayer ratios
filament_mixed_sublayer_ratios.tooltip: Comma-separated ratio values summing to 1.0, e.g. "0.7,0.3"

filament_mixed_gradient.label: Mixed filament gradient
filament_mixed_gradient.tooltip: Enable Z-direction gradient mode for mixed filament sub-layers. When enabled, the sub-layer ratios vary linearly across layers.

filament_mixed_gradient_range.label: Mixed filament gradient range
filament_mixed_gradient_range.tooltip: Start and end ratios for the first component in gradient mode. Comma-separated pair, e.g. "0.10,0.90" means 10% to 90%.

filament_mixed_gradient_curve.label: Mixed filament gradient curve
filament_mixed_gradient_curve.tooltip: Optional Photoshop-style custom curve mapping Z progress to the first component ratio. Encoded as pipe-separated control points, either "x,y" (legacy) or "x,y,m_in,m_out" when a tangent override is needed (empty token or "nan" means use PCHIP default). x in [0,1]; y is clamped to the configured ratio range, e.g. "0,0.15|0.5,0.50|1,0.85". When empty, the linear gradient_range is used instead.

filament_mixed_gradient_per_part.label: Mixed filament per-part gradient
filament_mixed_gradient_per_part.tooltip: When gradient mode is enabled, apply the gradient to each part of an assembly independently rather than treating the whole assembly as one Z range.

filament_printable.label: Filament printable
filament_printable.tooltip: The filament is printable in extruder.

filament_extruder_compatibility.label: Filament-extruder compatibility
filament_extruder_compatibility.tooltip: A single 32-bit int encoding the compatibility level of a filament across all extruders (up to 10). Every 3 bits represent one extruder (bits [3*i, 3*i+2] for extruder i). 0: printable, 1: error, 2: critical warning, 3: warning, 4-7: reserved.

temperature_vitrification.label: Softening temperature
temperature_vitrification.tooltip: The material softens at this temperature, so when the bed temperature is equal to or greater than this, it's highly recommended to open the front door and/or remove the upper glass to avoid clogs.

filament_cost.label: Price
filament_cost.tooltip: Filament price, for statistical purposes only.

filament_vendor.label: Vendor
filament_vendor.tooltip: Vendor of filament. For show only.

infill_direction.label: Sparse infill direction
infill_direction.tooltip: This is the angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of lines.

solid_infill_direction.label: Solid infill direction
solid_infill_direction.tooltip: Angle for solid infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.

top_layer_direction.label: Top layer direction
top_layer_direction.tooltip:
Fixed angle for the top solid infill and ironing lines.
Set to -1 to follow the default solid infill direction.

bottom_layer_direction.label: Bottom layer line angle
bottom_layer_direction.tooltip: Fixed angle for bottom solid infill lines (-1 uses the default solid infill angle).

sparse_infill_density.label: Sparse infill density
sparse_infill_density.tooltip: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% turns all sparse infill into solid infill and internal solid infill pattern will be used.

align_infill_direction_to_model.label: Rotate infill with model
align_infill_direction_to_model.tooltip: Rotates infill, bridging, ironing, and top/bottom surface lines along with the model on the build plate, so part strength and surface grain stay consistent no matter how you orient it.

extra_solid_infills.label: Insert solid layers
extra_solid_infills.tooltip: Insert solid infill at specific layers. Use N to insert every Nth layer, N#K to insert K consecutive solid layers every N layers (K is optional, e.g. '5#' equals '5#1'), or a comma-separated list (e.g. 1,7,9) to insert at explicit layers. Layers are 1-based.

fill_multiline.label: Fill Multiline
fill_multiline.tooltip: Using multiple lines for the infill pattern, if supported by infill pattern.

tpms_adaptive.label: Adaptive density (experimental)
tpms_adaptive.tooltip:
Grades the Gyroid and TPMS infill inside the object: its cells grow from the surface of the object towards its center. The sparse infill density is used at the surface and the interior density at the center.
Distance warp, Smooth blend and Stepped shells follow the distance to the nearest surface, including the top and bottom, with the interior density at the point farthest from it:
 - Distance warp: one continuous pattern, stretched and sheared where the distance changes across directions, as in plates and long parts.
 - Smooth blend: the patterns of neighbouring densities blended into each other, with small loops where they meet.
 - Stepped shells: shells of the regular pattern at densities about 1.5 times apart, their lines joined along the shell boundaries.
 - Lobes: follows the 3D shape of the object, including its top and bottom. Every lobe, a part joined to the rest by a narrower neck, is graded towards its own center.
 - Normal Z, Y or X: follows the sections of the object normal to that axis, so the density does not change along it.

tpms_interior_density.label: Interior density
tpms_interior_density.tooltip: Density of the adaptive infill at the center of the object.

tpms_adaptive_gradient.label: Adaptive gradient
tpms_adaptive_gradient.tooltip:
How the density changes from the surface to the center of the object.
Linear: the density changes at a constant rate.
Quadratic: the density stays close to the sparse infill density near the surface and changes faster towards the center.
Exponential: the density changes quickly just below the surface and levels off towards the center.

gyroid_optimized.label: Z-buckling bias optimization (experimental)
gyroid_optimized.tooltip: Tightens the gyroid wave along the Z (vertical) axis at low infill density to shorten the effective vertical column length and improve Z-axis compression buckling resistance. Filament use is preserved. No effect at ~30% sparse infill density and above. Only applies when Sparse infill pattern is set to Gyroid.

sparse_infill_pattern.label: Sparse infill pattern
sparse_infill_pattern.tooltip: This is the line pattern for internal sparse infill.

sparse_infill_smooth_factor.label: Sparse infill smooth factor
sparse_infill_smooth_factor.tooltip: Controls how strongly sparse infill corners are rounded. 0% keeps the original sharp path, while 100% produces the largest possible curves between adjacent infill lines.

top_surface_acceleration.label: Top surface
top_surface_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration of top surface infill. Using a lower value may improve top surface quality.

nonplanar_fallback_top_acceleration.label: Planar fallback top surface
nonplanar_fallback_top_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of top surface infill on an object Auto prints in planar layers because it found no curved surface for it, while the top surface acceleration keeps the value the process raised it to. 0 uses the top surface acceleration.

nonplanar_raised_top_acceleration.label: Raised top surface
nonplanar_raised_top_acceleration.tooltip: The top surface acceleration the process raised for curved tops. The planar fallback top surface acceleration replaces only this value.

outer_wall_acceleration.label: Outer wall
outer_wall_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of outer wall: using a lower value can improve quality.

sparse_infill_acceleration.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of sparse infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

internal_solid_infill_acceleration.label: Internal solid infill
internal_solid_infill_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of internal solid infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

initial_layer_acceleration.label: First layer
initial_layer_acceleration.tooltip: This is the printing acceleration for the first layer. Using limited acceleration can improve build plate adhesion.

accel_to_decel_enable.label: Auto-adjust accel_to_decel
accel_to_decel_enable.tooltip: Lets PancakeSlicer automatically tune Klipper's max_accel_to_decel.

accel_to_decel_factor.label: Accel to decel ratio
accel_to_decel_factor.tooltip: Sets Klipper's max_accel_to_decel as a percentage of your printing acceleration.

default_junction_deviation.label: Junction Deviation
default_junction_deviation.tooltip: Marlin Firmware Junction Deviation (replaces the traditional XY Jerk setting).

initial_layer_travel_jerk.label: First layer travel
initial_layer_travel_jerk.tooltip:
Travel jerk of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Jerk.

initial_layer_line_width.label: First layer
initial_layer_line_width.tooltip: Line width of the first layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

initial_layer_print_height.label: First layer height
initial_layer_print_height.tooltip: Height of the first layer. Making the first layer height thicker can improve build plate adhesion.

initial_layer_speed.label: First layer
initial_layer_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for the first layer except for solid infill sections.

initial_layer_infill_speed.label: First layer infill
initial_layer_infill_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for solid infill parts of the first layer.

initial_layer_travel_speed.label: First layer travel speed
initial_layer_travel_speed.tooltip: Travel speed of the first layer.

slow_down_layers.label: Number of slow layers
slow_down_layers.tooltip: The first few layers are printed slower than normal. The speed is gradually increased in a linear fashion over the specified number of layers.

nozzle_temperature_initial_layer.label: First layer
nozzle_temperature_initial_layer.tooltip: Nozzle temperature for printing the first layer with this filament

full_fan_speed_layer.label: Full fan speed at layer
full_fan_speed_layer.tooltip: Fan speed will be ramped up linearly from zero at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" to maximum at layer "full_fan_speed_layer". "full_fan_speed_layer" will be ignored if lower than "close_fan_the_first_x_layers", in which case the fan will be running at maximum allowed speed at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" + 1.

initial_layer_fan_speed.label: First layer fan speed
initial_layer_fan_speed.tooltip:
Sets an exact fan speed for the first layer, overriding all other cooling settings. Useful for protecting 3D-printed toolhead parts (e.g. Voron-style ABS/ASA ducts) from a hot bed. A small amount of airflow cools the ducts down, without using full cooling that may in certain conditions hurt first-layer adhesion.
From the second layer onwards, normal cooling resumes.
If "Full fan speed at layer" is also set, the fan ramps smoothly from this value on the first layer up to your target by the chosen layer.
Only available when "No cooling for the first" is 0.
Set to -1 to disable it.

support_material_interface_fan_speed.label: Support interface fan speed
support_material_interface_fan_speed.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when printing support interfaces. Setting this parameter to a higher than regular speed reduces the layer binding strength between supports and the supported part, making them easier to separate.
Set to -1 to disable it.
This setting is overridden by disable_fan_first_layers.

internal_bridge_fan_speed.label: Internal bridges fan speed
internal_bridge_fan_speed.tooltip:
The part cooling fan speed used for all internal bridges. Set to -1 to use the overhang fan speed settings instead.

Reducing the internal bridges fan speed, compared to your regular fan speed, can help reduce part warping due to excessive cooling applied over a large surface for a prolonged period of time.

ironing_fan_speed.label: Ironing fan speed
ironing_fan_speed.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when ironing. Setting this parameter to a lower than regular speed reduces possible nozzle clogging due to the low volumetric flow rate, making the interface smoother.
Set to -1 to disable it.

filament_ironing_flow.label: Ironing flow
filament_ironing_flow.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing flow. This allows you to customize the ironing flow for each filament type. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

filament_ironing_spacing.label: Ironing line spacing
filament_ironing_spacing.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing line spacing. This allows you to customize the spacing between ironing lines for each filament type.

filament_ironing_inset.label: Ironing inset
filament_ironing_inset.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing inset. This allows you to customize the distance to keep from the edges when ironing for each filament type.

filament_ironing_speed.label: Ironing speed
filament_ironing_speed.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing speed. This allows you to customize the print speed of ironing lines for each filament type.

fuzzy_skin.label: Fuzzy skin
fuzzy_skin.tooltip: This setting makes the toolhead randomly jitter while printing walls so that the surface has a rough textured look. This setting controls the fuzzy position.

fuzzy_skin_thickness.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
fuzzy_skin_thickness.tooltip: The width of jittering: it’s recommended to keep this lower than the outer wall line width.

fuzzy_skin_point_distance.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
fuzzy_skin_point_distance.tooltip: The average distance between the random points introduced on each line segment.

fuzzy_skin_first_layer.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer
fuzzy_skin_first_layer.tooltip: Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer.

fuzzy_skin_mode.label: Fuzzy skin generator mode
fuzzy_skin_mode.tooltip:
Fuzzy skin generation mode. Works only with Arachne!
Displacement: Сlassic mode when the pattern is formed by shifting the nozzle sideways from the original path.
Extrusion: The mode when the pattern formed by the amount of extruded plastic. This is the fast and straight algorithm without unnecessary nozzle shake that gives a smooth pattern. But it is more useful for forming loose walls in the entire they array.
Combined: Joint mode [Displacement] + [Extrusion]. The appearance of the walls is similar to [Displacement] Mode, but it leaves no pores between the perimeters.

Attention! The [Extrusion] and [Combined] modes works only the fuzzy_skin_thickness parameter not more than the thickness of printed loop. At the same time, the width of the extrusion for a particular layer should also not be below a certain level. It is usually equal 15-25%% of a layer height. Therefore, the maximum fuzzy skin thickness with a perimeter width of 0.4 mm and a layer height of 0.2 mm will be 0.4-(0.2*0.25)=±0.35mm! If you enter a higher parameter than this, the error Flow::spacing() will displayed, and the model will not be sliced. You can choose this number until this error is repeated.

fuzzy_skin_noise_type.label: Fuzzy skin noise type
fuzzy_skin_noise_type.tooltip:
Noise type to use for fuzzy skin generation:
Classic: Classic uniform random noise.
Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture.
Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier.
Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. Creates marble-like textures.
Voronoi: Divides the surface into voronoi cells, and displaces each one by a random amount. Creates a patchwork texture.
Ripple: Uniform ripple pattern that ripples left and right of the original path. Repeating pattern, woven appearance.

fuzzy_skin_scale.label: Fuzzy skin feature size
fuzzy_skin_scale.tooltip: The base size of the coherent noise features, in mm. Higher values will result in larger features.

fuzzy_skin_octaves.label: Fuzzy Skin Noise Octaves
fuzzy_skin_octaves.tooltip: The number of octaves of coherent noise to use. Higher values increase the detail of the noise, but also increase computation time.

fuzzy_skin_persistence.label: Fuzzy skin noise persistence
fuzzy_skin_persistence.tooltip: The decay rate for higher octaves of the coherent noise. Lower values will result in smoother noise.

fuzzy_skin_ripples_per_layer.label: Number of ripples per layer
fuzzy_skin_ripples_per_layer.tooltip: Controls how many full cycles of ripples will be added per layer.

fuzzy_skin_ripple_offset.label: Ripple offset
fuzzy_skin_ripple_offset.tooltip:
Shifts the ripple phase forward along the print path by the specified percentage of a wavelength each layer period.
- 0% keeps every layer identical.
- 50% shifts the pattern by half a wavelength, effectively inverting the phase.
- 100% shifts the pattern by a full wavelength, returning to the original phase.

The shift is applied once every number of layers set by Layers between ripple offset, so layers within the same group are printed identically.

fuzzy_skin_layers_between_ripple_offset.label: Layers between ripple offset
fuzzy_skin_layers_between_ripple_offset.tooltip:
Specifies how many consecutive layers share the same ripple phase before the offset is applied.
For example:
- 1 = Layer 1 is printed with the base ripple pattern, then layer 2 is shifted by the configured offset, then layer 3 returns to the base pattern, and so on.
- 3 = Layers 1 to 3 are printed with the base ripple pattern, then layers 4 to 6 are shifted by the configured offset, then layers 7 to 9 return to the base pattern, etc.

filter_out_gap_fill.label: Filter out tiny gaps
filter_out_gap_fill.tooltip: Don't print gap fill with a length is smaller than the threshold specified (in mm). This setting applies to top, bottom and solid infill and, if using the classic perimeter generator, to wall gap fill.

gap_infill_speed.label: Gap infill
gap_infill_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for gap infill. Gaps usually have irregular line width and should be printed more slowly.

precise_z_height.label: Precise Z height
precise_z_height.tooltip: Enable this to get precise Z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.

adaptive_layer_height_error.label: Adaptive layer height
adaptive_layer_height_error.tooltip: Automatically adjusts layer height so stair-stepping on sloped surfaces stays within this distance of the true shape. Vertical walls keep your standard layer height, shallow slopes get thinner layers, and flat tops or bridges land cleanly on a layer boundary. Set to 0 to turn off. (Skipped when using manual variable layer heights, height modifiers, prime towers, organic tree supports, or vase mode.)

overhang_layer_contact.label: Overhang layer contact
overhang_layer_contact.tooltip: Thinner layers under overhangs: where a sloped underside would leave the outer wall resting on less than this share of its width on the layer below, the layers there get thin enough to keep it, down to the printer's minimum layer height. Undersides too flat for that are left to bridges and supports. Like the adaptive layer height, it also lands flat surfaces on layer boundaries and is not applied in the cases listed there, nor under the non-planar modes, whose curved overhangs print the undersides. 0 disables.

enable_arc_fitting.label: Arc fitting
enable_arc_fitting.tooltip:
Enable this to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. The fitting tolerance is same as the resolution.

Note: For Klipper machines, this option is recommended to be disabled. Klipper does not benefit from arc commands as these are split again into line segments by the firmware. This results in a reduction in surface quality as line segments are converted to arcs by the slicer and then back to line segments by the firmware.

gcode_add_line_number.label: Add line number
gcode_add_line_number.tooltip: Enable this to add line number(Nx) at the beginning of each G-code line.

scan_first_layer.label: Scan first layer
scan_first_layer.tooltip: Enable this to allow the camera on the printer to check the quality of the first layer.

enable_power_loss_recovery.label: Power Loss Recovery
enable_power_loss_recovery.tooltip: Choose how to control power loss recovery. When set to Printer configuration, the slicer will not emit power loss recovery G-code and will leave the printer's configuration unchanged. Applicable to Bambu Lab or Marlin 2 firmware based printers.

nozzle_type.label: Nozzle type
nozzle_type.tooltip: The metallic material of the nozzle: This determines the abrasive resistance of the nozzle and what kind of filament can be printed.

nozzle_hrc.label: Nozzle HRC
nozzle_hrc.tooltip: The nozzle's hardness. Zero means no checking for nozzle hardness during slicing.

printer_structure.label: Printer structure
printer_structure.tooltip: The physical arrangement and components of a printing device.

best_object_pos.label: Default auto-arrange position
best_object_pos.tooltip: Preferred [0, 1] bed coordinates where auto-arrange centers parts.

auxiliary_fan.label: Auxiliary part cooling fan
auxiliary_fan.tooltip: Enable if your printer has a side/auxiliary part cooling fan (M106 P2 S0-255).

fan_direction.label: Fan direction
fan_direction.tooltip: Cooling fan direction of the printer

fan_speedup_time.tooltip:
Start the fan this number of seconds earlier than its target start time (you can use fractional seconds). It assumes infinite acceleration for this time estimation, and will only take into account G1 and G0 moves (arc fitting is unsupported).
It won't move fan commands from custom G-code (they act as a sort of 'barrier').
It won't move fan commands into the start G-code if the 'only custom start G-code' is activated.
Use 0 to deactivate.

fan_speedup_overhangs.label: Only overhangs
fan_speedup_overhangs.tooltip: Will only take into account the delay for the cooling of overhangs.

fan_kickstart.label: Fan kick-start time
fan_kickstart.tooltip:
Emit a max fan speed command for this amount of seconds before reducing to target speed to kick-start the cooling fan.
This is useful for fans where a low PWM/power may be insufficient to get the fan started spinning from a stop, or to get the fan up to speed faster.
Set to 0 to deactivate.
