part_cooling_fan_min_pwm.label: Minimum non-zero part cooling fan speed
part_cooling_fan_min_pwm.tooltip:
Some part-cooling fans cannot start spinning when commanded below a certain PWM duty cycle. When set above 0, any non-zero part-cooling fan command will be raised to at least this percentage so the fan reliably starts. A fan command of 0 (fan off) is always honoured exactly. This clamp is applied after every other fan calculation (first-layer ramp, layer-time interpolation, overhang/bridge/support-interface/ironing overrides), so scaling still operates within the range [this value, 100%].
If your firmware already disables the fan below a threshold (for example Klipper's [fan] off_below: 0.10 shuts the fan off whenever the commanded duty cycle is below 10%), this option and the firmware threshold should ideally be set to the same value. Matching them (e.g. off_below: 0.10 in Klipper and 10% here) guarantees the slicer never emits a non-zero value that the firmware would silently drop, and the fan never receives a value below the one you know it can actually spool at.
Set to 0 to deactivate.

support_chamber_temp_control.label: Support controlling chamber temperature
support_chamber_temp_control.tooltip:
This option is enabled if machine support controlling chamber temperature
G-code command: M141 S(0-255)

support_air_filtration.label: Support air filtration
support_air_filtration.tooltip:
Enable this if printer support air filtration
G-code command: M106 P3 S(0-255)

cooling_filter_enabled.label: Use cooling filter
cooling_filter_enabled.tooltip: Enable this if printer support cooling filter

gcode_flavor.label: G-code flavor
gcode_flavor.tooltip: What kind of G-code the printer is compatible with.

gcode_skip_config_block.label: Skip G-code config block
gcode_skip_config_block.tooltip: Do not write the CONFIG_BLOCK (slicer configuration key/value pairs) into the G-code file. This can help with printers whose firmware crashes when parsing these comment lines (e.g. Anycubic go-klipper). Note: the G-code file will no longer contain slicer settings, so importing it back into OrcaSlicer will not restore the configuration.

pellet_modded_printer.label: Pellet Modded Printer
pellet_modded_printer.tooltip: Enable this option if your printer uses pellets instead of filaments.

support_multi_bed_types.label: Support multi bed types
support_multi_bed_types.tooltip: Enable this option if you want to use multiple bed types.

gcode_label_objects.label: Label objects
gcode_label_objects.tooltip: Enable this to add comments into the G-code labeling print moves with what object they belong to, which is useful for the Octoprint CancelObject plug-in. This setting is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

exclude_object.label: Exclude objects
exclude_object.tooltip: Enable this option to add EXCLUDE OBJECT command in G-code.

gcode_comments.label: Verbose G-code
gcode_comments.tooltip: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

infill_combination.label: Infill combination
infill_combination.tooltip: Automatically combine sparse infill of several layers to print together in order to reduce time. Walls are still printed with original layer height.

infill_shift_step.label: Infill shift step
infill_shift_step.tooltip: This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

sparse_infill_rotate_template.label: Sparse infill rotation template
sparse_infill_rotate_template.tooltip: Rotate the sparse infill direction per layer using a template of angles. Enter comma-separated degrees (e.g., '0,30,60,90'). Angles are applied in order by layer and repeat when the list ends. Advanced syntax is supported: '+5' rotates +5° every layer; '+5#5' rotates +5° every 5 layers. See the Wiki for details. When a template is set, the standard infill direction setting is ignored. Note: some infill patterns (e.g., Gyroid) control rotation themselves; use with care.

solid_infill_rotate_template.label: Solid infill rotation template
solid_infill_rotate_template.tooltip: This parameter adds a rotation of solid infill direction to each layer according to the specified template. The template is a comma-separated list of angles in degrees, e.g. '0,90'. The first angle is applied to the first layer, the second angle to the second layer, and so on. If there are more layers than angles, the angles will be repeated. Note that not all solid infill patterns support rotation.

skeleton_infill_density.label: Skeleton infill density
skeleton_infill_density.tooltip: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densities, their skeleton areas will develop overlapping sections. Default is as same as infill density.

skin_infill_density.label: Skin infill density
skin_infill_density.tooltip: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, this area will not be split into two separate regions. Default is as same as infill density.

skin_infill_depth.label: Skin infill depth
skin_infill_depth.tooltip: The parameter sets the depth of skin.

infill_lock_depth.label: Infill lock depth
infill_lock_depth.tooltip: The parameter sets the overlapping depth between the interior and skin.

skin_infill_line_width.label: Skin line width
skin_infill_line_width.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skin paths.

skeleton_infill_line_width.label: Skeleton line width
skeleton_infill_line_width.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skeleton paths.

symmetric_infill_y_axis.label: Symmetric infill Y axis
symmetric_infill_y_axis.tooltip: If the model has two parts that are symmetric about the Y axis, and you want these parts to have symmetric textures, please click this option on one of the parts.

infill_complete_top.label: Fill pattern tops
infill_complete_top.tooltip: Choose this option if you want to completely fill in the tops of the infill pattern

infill_combination_max_layer_height.label: Infill combination - Max layer height
infill_combination_max_layer_height.tooltip:
Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived by dividing this value with the layer height and rounded down to the nearest decimal.

Use either absolute mm values (eg. 0.32mm for a 0.4mm nozzle) or % values (eg 80%). This value must not be larger than the nozzle diameter.

lateral_lattice_angle_1.label: Lateral lattice angle 1
lateral_lattice_angle_1.tooltip: The angle of the first set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

lateral_lattice_angle_2.label: Lateral lattice angle 2
lateral_lattice_angle_2.tooltip: The angle of the second set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

infill_overhang_angle.label: Infill overhang angle
infill_overhang_angle.tooltip: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.

lightning_overhang_angle.label: Lightning overhang angle
lightning_overhang_angle.tooltip: Maximum overhang angle for Lightning infill support propagation.

lightning_prune_angle.label: Prune angle
lightning_prune_angle.tooltip:
Controls how aggressively short or unsupported Lightning branches are pruned.
This angle is converted internally to a per-layer distance.

lightning_straightening_angle.label: Straightening angle
lightning_straightening_angle.tooltip: Maximum straightening angle used to simplify Lightning branches.

infill_anchor.label: Sparse infill anchor length
infill_anchor.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max.
Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

infill_anchor_max.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
infill_anchor_max.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter.
If set to 0, the old algorithm for infill connection will be used, it should create the same result as with 1000 & 0.

sparse_infill_filament_id.label: Infill
sparse_infill_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print internal sparse infill.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

sparse_infill_line_width.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_line_width.tooltip: Line width of internal sparse infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

infill_wall_overlap.label: Infill/wall overlap
infill_wall_overlap.tooltip: This allows the infill area to be enlarged slightly to overlap with walls for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top surfaces.

top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap.label: Top/Bottom solid infill/wall overlap
top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap.tooltip: Top solid infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding and to minimize the appearance of pinholes where the top infill meets the walls. A value of 25-30% is a good starting point, minimizing the appearance of pinholes. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill.

sparse_infill_speed.label: Sparse infill
sparse_infill_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for internal sparse infill.

interface_shells.label: Interface shells
interface_shells.tooltip: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material.

mmu_segmented_region_max_width.label: Maximum width of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_max_width.tooltip: Maximum width of a segmented region. A value of 0 disables this feature.

mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.tooltip: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. It will be ignored if "mmu_segmented_region_max_width" is zero or if "mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth" is bigger than "mmu_segmented_region_max_width". Zero disables this feature.

interlocking_beam.label: Use beam interlocking
interlocking_beam.tooltip: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

interlocking_beam_width.label: Interlocking beam width
interlocking_beam_width.tooltip: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

interlocking_beam_layer_count.label: Interlocking beam layers
interlocking_beam_layer_count.tooltip: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

interlocking_depth.label: Interlocking depth
interlocking_depth.tooltip: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

interlocking_boundary_avoidance.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
interlocking_boundary_avoidance.tooltip: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

ironing_type.label: Ironing type
ironing_type.tooltip: Ironing uses a small flow to print at the same height of a surface to make flat surfaces smoother. This setting controls which layers are being ironed.

ironing_pattern.label: Ironing Pattern
ironing_pattern.tooltip: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

ironing_flow.label: Ironing flow
ironing_flow.tooltip: This is the amount of material to be extruded during ironing. It is relative to the flow of normal layer height. Too high a value will result in overextrusion on the surface.

ironing_spacing.label: Ironing line spacing
ironing_spacing.tooltip: This is the distance between the lines used for ironing.

ironing_inset.label: Ironing inset
ironing_inset.tooltip: The distance to keep from the edges. A value of 0 sets this to half of the nozzle diameter.

ironing_speed.label: Ironing speed
ironing_speed.tooltip: This is the print speed for ironing lines.

ironing_angle.label: Ironing angle offset
ironing_angle.tooltip: The angle of ironing lines offset from the top surface.

ironing_angle_fixed.label: Fixed ironing angle
ironing_angle_fixed.tooltip: Use a fixed absolute angle for ironing.

ironing_expansion.label: Ironing expansion
ironing_expansion.tooltip: Expand or contract the ironing area.

zaa_minimize_perimeter_height.label: Minimize wall height angle
zaa_minimize_perimeter_height.tooltip:
Reduce the height of top-surface perimeters to match the model edge height.
Affects perimeters with a slope less than this angle (degrees).
A reasonable value is 35. Set to 0 to disable.

zaa_dont_alternate_fill_direction.label: Don't alternate fill direction
zaa_dont_alternate_fill_direction.tooltip: Disable alternating fill direction when using Z contouring.

zaa_min_z.label: Minimum Z height
zaa_min_z.tooltip:
Minimum Z-layer height.
Also controls the slicing plane.

zaa_mid_layer_slice.label: Slice at mid-layer
zaa_mid_layer_slice.tooltip: Slice each layer at its middle, as without Z contouring, and move top surface lines up or down by up to half a layer onto the surface. Walls and steep faces then print as flat layers do, instead of from a slice near the bottom of the layer. Default: off.

top_texture.label: Top texture
top_texture.tooltip: A grip relief on top surfaces, grown through the last three solid layers under each top and faded out near its edges, so it stands on the layers below it. Ribs are rounded diagonal ridges, Knurl a diamond pattern of rounded bumps. The relief adds to the model's height. Default: None.

top_texture_depth.label: Top texture depth
top_texture_depth.tooltip: Height of the top texture's ridges or bumps over the flat top. Default: 0.18 mm.

top_texture_pitch.label: Top texture pitch
top_texture_pitch.tooltip: Distance between the top texture's ridges or bumps. Default: 5 mm.

nonplanar_top_shells.label: Curved top shells
nonplanar_top_shells.tooltip: Number of curved shells printed along the model's top surface. 0 prints none; -1 chooses the number for each curved area from its slope and size, as Auto does. Default: 0. Unit: shells. Auto replaces this count with 2 to 6 shells per area, capped by the planar top and available depth.

nonplanar_bottom_shells.label: Curved bottom shells
nonplanar_bottom_shells.tooltip: Number of curved shells printed along the model's underside, usually over support. 0 prints none; -1 prints one nozzle diameter of skin, 2 to 6 shells. With height bands, undersides steeper than 60° keep their planar walls. Auto prints them only with supports on, under undersides of 10° or less. Default: 0. Unit: shells. Auto ignores this count and chooses 2 to 6 shells from nozzle diameter and shell height, only with supports enabled, on undersides up to 10 degrees.

nonplanar_shell_layer_height.label: Curved shell layer height
nonplanar_shell_layer_height.tooltip: Vertical thickness of each curved shell. 0 uses the layer height. At most 75% of the nozzle diameter. Default: 0. Unit: mm. Auto retains a positive value; 0 derives the shell height from the layer profile.

nonplanar_max_slope.label: Non-planar maximum slope
nonplanar_max_slope.tooltip: Curved shells and curved layers flatten wherever the surface is steeper than this. With the Z contouring or Planar fallback the head's own slope limit applies too, and areas flattened by more than the surface tolerance use the fallback. Curved overhangs bend by at most this angle, 40° when it is 0. 0 adds no limit. Default: 0. Unit: degrees. Auto ignores this cap for top and bottom shells; head clearance and the steep planar admission rule still apply.

nonplanar_max_surface_error.label: Non-planar surface tolerance
nonplanar_max_surface_error.tooltip: Largest vertical gap allowed between the model and the curved shells. With the Z contouring or Planar fallback, areas the head cannot follow more closely use the fallback. With height bands the shells follow the surface, and adaptive curved shell height may thicken the outermost bead until its step reaches this tolerance. On rotary printers a top line tilts where an upright line would stand prouder than this. Auto chooses its own value per area. Default: 0.05. Unit: mm. Auto replaces this tolerance with one quarter of the shell height, clamped to 0.02 to 0.1 mm.

nonplanar_min_patch_area.label: Non-planar minimum patch area
nonplanar_min_patch_area.tooltip: With the Z contouring or Planar fallback, curved areas smaller than this, seen from above, use the fallback. Height bands keep every area. Default: 16. Unit: mm². Auto derives its own area threshold; height bands bypass the area cut.

nonplanar_top_pattern.label: Curved top pattern
nonplanar_top_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern of the curved shells. Contour follows the surface's level lines: a spiral on round tops such as domes, straight lines elsewhere, and the only pattern that stays continuous across height bands. Rectilinear uses the solid infill direction. Concentric follows nested outlines. Default: Contour. Unit: unitless choice. Auto chooses Contour, except where an object, modifier or height range overrides the top pattern.

nonplanar_top_direction.label: Curved top direction
nonplanar_top_direction.tooltip: Angle of the lines on curved tops. Auto (-2): along each top's longest extent, the fewest lines and turns. -1: along the surface's level lines. A Custom angle is used exactly as set, in every method. Default: Auto. Unit: degrees.

nonplanar_surface_spacing.label: Curved line spacing along surface
nonplanar_surface_spacing.tooltip: Space the lines of the curved shells by the line width measured along the surface, not from above. On slopes the lines lie closer and each carries less material, so the shell keeps its thickness. Applies to line patterns, not to the spirals and height-band lines of the Contour pattern. Default: on. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_spiral_top.label: Spiral curved tops
nonplanar_spiral_top.tooltip: Print the outermost shell of a round curved top, such as a dome or a bowl with a median slope of 12° or more, as one spiral from the rim to the apex, with no seam and no retraction. In spiral vase mode, in Auto and Manual, the wall carries on into a closed curved lid in the same extrusion unless curved bottom shells are printed. Otherwise Auto keeps the rings. Default: on. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto disables this spiral except for the spiral-vase lid.

nonplanar_sublayer_walls.label: Half-height outer walls
nonplanar_sublayer_walls.tooltip: In Auto, Off and Curved tops (3-axis), print the outer wall as two lines of half the layer height where the face is steeper than 25 degrees, vertical walls included, each at the outline of its own half of the layer, so the wall shows half the layer's ridges and a slope half its stair. The lower line prints at the end of the layer below. Slopes near 45 degrees are taken first, until the extra lines would add about 40 % of the part's estimated extrusion time; on typical parts every outer wall fits, for 5 to 20 % more print time. Walls already raised onto a top by Z contouring keep their single line.

nonplanar_flow_mod.label: Non-planar flow modulation
nonplanar_flow_mod.tooltip: Extrude each curved shell line by the bead the nozzle can lay there: the thickness above the material below, how far the flat nozzle tip reaches on a slope, and a smooth change along the line. Thin and steep parts of the shells print slower, within the filament's maximum volumetric speed. Default: on. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_adaptive_bands.label: Adaptive curved shell height
nonplanar_adaptive_bands.tooltip: Vary the thickness of the curved top shells with the surface, as adaptive layer height does for flat layers: thin outer beads where slope or curvature would leave steps larger than the non-planar surface tolerance, thick beads on gentle slopes, from 0.2 to 0.75 of the nozzle diameter (0.6 for the outermost bead). The shells keep their total thickness, so gentle areas need fewer of them. Height bands only. Where the clearance repair finds the head hitting printed material, the shells there keep a uniform thickness. Default: off. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_infill_depth.label: Curved infill depth
nonplanar_infill_depth.tooltip: With height bands, this much sparse infill under the curved top shells follows the surface too, so the shells rest on a curved base instead of the steps of the flat layers. The step to the flat layers moves into the sparse infill, where it does not show. Rounded to whole shell layers. 0 curves only the shells. Manual only: Auto curves only the shells. Default: 2. Unit: mm. Auto overrides this depth with 0 mm.

nonplanar_strength_roads.label: Load-aligned curved infill
nonplanar_strength_roads.tooltip: Lay the hidden curved layers for strength: their infill runs along and across the direction that carries the load (where the surface curves least, else the part's long axis), turning 90° from layer to layer, and each curved layer under the top shells gets a curved wall along its edge instead of ending against the flat layers. The visible top shell keeps its own pattern. Default: on. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_ironing.label: Curved ironing
nonplanar_ironing.tooltip: Iron the curved top after its last shell, with the process ironing pattern, spacing, flow, speed and inset. An ironing type other than "No ironing" irons curved tops too. Ironing stops where the slope would press the flat nozzle tip through the shell, and flexible filaments are not ironed. Auto irons a curved area only when ironing is asked for and the flat nozzle tip fits its curvature; an object, modifier or height range set to "No ironing" irons none. Default: off. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto admits requested ironing only where the nozzle land fits the curvature, and disables it on rotary printers.

nonplanar_top_finish_flow.label: Curved top flow ratio
nonplanar_top_finish_flow.tooltip: Flow of the outermost curved shell, on top of the top surface flow ratio. Slightly less material leaves the visible surface without ridges. With non-planar flow modulation off, this shell also slows on slopes steeper than 25°, down to 0.7 of its speed. Default: 0.95. Unit: unitless multiplier. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_tilt_flow.label: Curved top flow by slope
nonplanar_tilt_flow.tooltip: Flow of the curved top shells by surface slope, at 0, 10, 20, 30 and 40°, interpolated between and held beyond 40°. A tilted bead wets the layer below differently from a level one. Calibration > Non-planar > Tilted-bead flow measures these values. Default: 1, 1, 1, 1, 1. Unit: unitless multipliers at 0/10/20/30/40 degrees. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_top_speed_factor.label: Curved top speed
nonplanar_top_speed_factor.tooltip: Speed of the visible curved top lines. Below 100%, a share of the speed each line would otherwise run after the slope, Z and flow limits; above, a share of the top surface speed, under the same limits. Calibration > Non-planar > Curved-top quality measures it. Default: 100. Unit: percent. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_top_fan_boost.label: Curved top fan boost
nonplanar_top_fan_boost.tooltip: Extra part cooling on the visible curved top lines, as a share of the way from the layer's fan speed to the overhang fan speed. 0 leaves the fan to curved line cooling; 100 runs those lines at the overhang fan speed. Needs curved line cooling. Calibration > Non-planar > Curved-top quality measures it. Default: 0. Unit: percent. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_overhangs.label: Curved overhangs
nonplanar_overhangs.tooltip: Print overhangs too steep for flat layers without support: under the overhang the layers bend down and away from the supported part, so each layer reaches only a fraction of a line width beyond the one below. Covers undersides down to flat roofs, and bridges that curved bridges do not take. The layers bend by at most the non-planar maximum slope, 40° when it is 0. With supports and the curved support interface on, supported overhangs get that interface instead. Auto always prints them and leaves support out under them. Default: off. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto enables curved overhangs regardless of this switch.

nonplanar_bridges.label: Curved bridges
nonplanar_bridges.tooltip: Print bridges spanning 4 to 45 mm as shallow curves that sag 1/80 of the span from both ends, the shape the hot bead settles into, instead of straight lines that droop after they are laid. The layers above level the sag out with thicker beads. Not with supports on, which would stand in the sag. Auto prints them whenever supports are off. Default: off. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto enables curved bridges when supports are off regardless of this switch.

nonplanar_fallback.label: Non-planar fallback
nonplanar_fallback.tooltip: How to print top areas the head cannot follow in one curved pass. Height bands prints every top area curved, in thin bands from the lowest up, so the head never meets material printed before. Z contouring and Planar curve only the areas the head can print in any order; Z contouring smooths the steps of the flat layers left elsewhere, Planar prints them as usual. Quality > Z contouring stays separate. Default: Height bands. Unit: unitless choice. Auto always selects Height bands.

nonplanar_full_conformal_max_thickness.label: Curved thin-part thickness
nonplanar_full_conformal_max_thickness.tooltip: Print parts up to this thick entirely in curved layers that blend from the underside to the top, walls and infill included, with no flat layers: wing skins, domes, canopies, panels. Thicker or steeper areas stay planar. 0 prints none in Manual and Multiplanar. Auto prints them only on a model with holes in its surface (open edges on more than 1 in 100 facets), up to this thickness or 15 shell layers at 0; on a closed model, none. Not in spiral vase mode. Default: 0. Unit: mm. Auto uses a positive value only on open meshes, or 15 shell layers at 0; closed meshes use none.

nonplanar_surface_resolution.label: Non-planar surface resolution
nonplanar_surface_resolution.tooltip: Grid spacing used to sample curved surfaces. Smaller values follow finer detail but take more time and memory. Default: 0.2. Unit: mm. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_max_patch_height.label: Maximum curved band height
nonplanar_max_patch_height.tooltip: Height of the bands the curved top shells print in. With height bands, 0 uses the head's reach (how far it can sink beside material already printed) and a smaller value makes the bands shorter. With the Z contouring or Planar fallback, a positive value splits tall areas into bands this high and 0 leaves them whole. Curved bottom bands keep their own limit. Default: 0. Unit: mm. Auto replaces this cap with a head-derived limit; height bands also obey the head reach.

nonplanar_wave.label: Non-planar waves
nonplanar_wave.tooltip: Ripple the top shells, the whole object above a flat base, or sparse infill. Works on fixed-head printers with any non-planar mode. Rotary printers ignore this setting. Default: Off. Unit: unitless choice.

nonplanar_wave_amplitude.label: Wave amplitude
nonplanar_wave_amplitude.tooltip: Peak height of the waves. Sparse infill is limited to half the layer height. Top shells are limited to half a layer height for nozzle-land clearance. Default: 0.4. Unit: mm.

nonplanar_wave_wavelength.label: Wave wavelength
nonplanar_wave_wavelength.tooltip: Distance between wave crests. Longer waves are gentler. Default: 30. Unit: mm.

nonplanar_wave_pattern.label: Wave pattern
nonplanar_wave_pattern.tooltip: Waves run in one direction, ripples spread from the object's centre, and crosshatch waves cross in X and Y. Default: Waves. Unit: unitless choice.

nonplanar_wave_direction.label: Wave direction
nonplanar_wave_direction.tooltip: Direction of the wave field in the XY plane. Used by the Waves pattern. Default: 45. Unit: degrees.

nonplanar_region_source.label: Non-planar regions
nonplanar_region_source.tooltip: Auto detects curved tops. Paint only uses enforced areas. Blocked areas always stay planar.

nonplanar_mode.label: Non-planar mode
nonplanar_mode.tooltip:
Flat layers: every layer flat, as in standard OrcaSlicer; fastest.
Auto: on a fixed print head, Smooth morph for a single gentle curved top (a low dome, wave, ramp or lid) and Curved tops otherwise; on a printer with rotary axes, curved layers wherever the head clears them.
Manual: the curved settings below, as set.
Multiplanar: the part in chunks of flat layers, each chunk tilted so its overhangs need less support.
Rotary curved layers: the whole part in curved layers, the table tilting so each line is laid level under the nozzle. Needs two rotary axes.
One-shot field (advanced): rotary curved layers whose layer field is solved for the part from its surface error, support, print time and head clearance, within a minute.
Curved tops: bends the top layers (Curved top layers, 3 by default) over every gentle top the print head clears; flat tops get mid-layer Z smoothing.
Smooth morph: bends every layer from the flat base up to the top; lowest error on domes and lids, up to about 1.4x flat time.
Slant: the whole part in layers tilted from the bed, as on a belt printer, on a fixed 3-axis head: a flat first layer, then each layer tilts a little more up to the slant angle; smoother faces that slope the same way as the layers, flat tops step.
Conformal layers (experimental): the top shells follow every top up to 20 degrees at a constant thickness, each top one whole layer, sliced on the model itself; flat layers elsewhere, printed in bands the head clears.
 Default: Flat layers. Unit: unitless choice. Auto is selected explicitly by a process or object; it does not replace the stored mode.

nonplanar_continuous_top.label: Continuous curved top
nonplanar_continuous_top.tooltip: Generate a connected stripe field over each curved top to reduce transitions. Experimental; normal clearance checks still apply.

nonplanar_curved_max_angle.label: Maximum curved top angle
nonplanar_curved_max_angle.tooltip: Steepest surface every curved slicing method tries to follow. Where the head would collide deeper than the collision tolerance, the angle steps down (40, 35, 30, 25, 20, 16, 12) and the slice reports the angle it used. Supported range: 0–45 degrees. Default: 30. Unit: degrees.

nonplanar_curved_top_layers.label: Curved top layers
nonplanar_curved_top_layers.tooltip: How many layers on top follow the curved surface. A number is used exactly as set; only a head collision beyond the Head clearance limits flattens a patch. 0 (Auto): each method's own count, Curved tops 3, Conformal layers and Smooth morph the profile's top shell layers. Default: Auto. Unit: layers.

nonplanar_deform.label: Curved layers through the whole part
nonplanar_deform.tooltip:
Print the whole part in curved layers, walls, infill, top and bottom, in height bands the head clears.
Chosen explicitly (any value but Auto and Off), the outer walls on faces steeper than 25° stay planar, with their half-height beads, around the curved inside; the bands are then 1 mm tall, which costs time.
Auto (recommended): in Auto mode, only where it measures better than curved top shells alone.
Column field: every layer stretched column by column so the top lies on one layer. Best on domes; flat and saddle tops cross thin layers.
QuickCurve (experimental): one smooth surface fitted to the top, every layer above a short base that surface shifted up, all of one thickness. Best on low parts with gently curved tops; a tall dome's rim still crosses layers.
Conical (experimental): shallow cones sloping down outward from the part's centre, for overhangs that lean outward. Tops cross the cones.
Optimized field (experimental): curved layers solved to follow the top and lean under overhangs within the head's reach.
Off: never. A layer source that cannot slice a part falls back to Auto's curved shells with a warning. Default: Auto. Unit: unitless choice. In Auto mode, Auto compares the column-field slice with the shells: a whole-surface gain that pays for its time, no worse top and bounded added overhang. The other values force their field.

multiplanar_max_planes.label: Multiplanar maximum planes
multiplanar_max_planes.tooltip: Most cut planes in one object. Each plane starts a new chunk of flat layers.

multiplanar_overhang_threshold.label: Multiplanar overhang threshold
multiplanar_overhang_threshold.tooltip: Undersides flatter than this, measured from their own layers, count as overhangs. Multiplanar places its cut planes to remove them; rotary curved layers tilt until they clear it by 5°. Auto uses it too when it plans chunks on a rotary printer.

nonplanar_slant_angle.label: Slant angle
nonplanar_slant_angle.tooltip: Tilt of Slant's layers from the bed, used as set. Only an angle at which the print head would hit the part is lowered, to the steepest it clears (on an A1 mini about 25° front to back, 7° left to right). Default: 15. Unit: degrees.

nonplanar_slant_direction.label: Slant direction
nonplanar_slant_direction.tooltip: Direction about Z, counterclockwise from +X, toward which Slant's layers face and descend. -1: the direction of 8 that leaves the least stair-step and overhang on this part. Default: -1. Unit: degrees.

nonplanar_slant_start_height.label: Slant start height
nonplanar_slant_start_height.tooltip: Height of the last flat layer before Slant's layers start to tilt. 0: right after the first layer, as low as the print head allows (an upright head stays above everything it prints). Without morphing, a negative height lowers the tilted start plane by that much, below the bed, so tilted layers reach further down the part. Default: 0. Unit: mm.

nonplanar_slant_morph_layers.label: Slant morph layers
nonplanar_slant_morph_layers.tooltip: Slant morphing: layers over which Slant bends from flat to the full angle, each a little more than the one below. A wide part or a steep angle takes more, so that every layer stays between 0.2 and 0.8 of the nozzle diameter thick. 0 turns morphing off: the part is cut by the tilted start plane, flat layers below it with their top finished to the plane, tilted layers above it. Default: 0.

nonplanar_auto_support.label: Add support where a part would float
nonplanar_auto_support.tooltip: With support off, Auto and One-shot still add tree support, critical regions only, where the part would otherwise print in the air (floating regions, a floating cantilever), and say so. Off: no support unless you enable it.

nonplanar_support_interface.label: Curved support interface
nonplanar_support_interface.tooltip: Under a curved underside, print the top support interface along the underside, offset down by the top Z distance, and the first bottom layer over it as a curved layer. The support body stays planar. At most two interface layers are curved, fewer where the head's reach requires. Every non-planar mode but Off; needs a print head on the printer's Non-planar page. With supports on it replaces curved overhangs, except in Auto, which curves it only under curved overhangs, curved bottom shells and undersides of 10° or less. Default: on. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto retains this switch and restricts curved interfaces to the curved underside areas it admits.

nonplanar_steep_skin.label: Tilted skin on steep faces
nonplanar_steep_skin.tooltip: On a printer with a tilting table or head, replace the outer wall of steep faces (39° to 80° from horizontal, such as chamfers) with roads laid up the face with the nozzle tilted toward it, after the object's last layer. This removes the layer stair on those faces. Only faces bounded by edges are skinned, and only when they make at least 300 mm² and 10% of the visible surface; curved and organic surfaces keep their planar wall. Needs non-planar mode Auto. Default: off. Unit: unitless on/off.

nonplanar_oneshot_routes.label: One-shot tilted routes
nonplanar_oneshot_routes.tooltip: On a printer with a tilting table or head, non-planar mode One-shot also offers to print overhanging branches in tilted planar chunks, as Auto plans them, and picks a chunked print over the planar one only where it is better on the same objective and within the same time limit. Printers without rotary axes ignore it. Default: on. Unit: unitless on/off.

nonplanar_oneshot_fan_step.label: One-shot route joint step
nonplanar_oneshot_fan_step.tooltip: Where two chunks of a One-shot tilted route meet, the layers turn from one direction to the other in steps of at most this angle, so the joint shows as a gradual turn instead of a line. Smaller steps make the joint less visible and add a few layers. Where a route planned this way would exceed One-shot's time limit, it is planned again with 10 degree steps. Printers without rotary axes ignore it. Default: 7. Unit: degrees.

nonplanar_atom_toolpath.label: Atomizer toolpath
nonplanar_atom_toolpath.tooltip: Path of a toolpath written by Atomizer (.poses or .npz) for this object. When set, the object prints that whole-part curved toolpath instead of its layers. Empty slices normally. Default: empty. Unit: file path. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_field_file.label: Layer field file
nonplanar_field_file.tooltip: Path of a layer field (.npz, npfield v1) for this object. When set, rotary curved layers follow that field instead of solving their own. Empty solves the field. Default: empty. Unit: file path.

nonplanar_collision_check.label: Head clearance check
nonplanar_collision_check.tooltip: Check that the print head clears material printed before. Off skips it, Warn reports moves that would hit, Block export refuses to export while curved moves still hit. Auto checks at least as Warn. Only the parts of the machine in the head model are checked; the Clearance view lists what it leaves out. Default: Warn. Unit: unitless choice. Auto raises Off to Warn and retains Block export.

nonplanar_repair_iterations.label: Clearance repair passes
nonplanar_repair_iterations.tooltip: When the clearance check finds the head hitting printed material, regenerate the curved shells and the G-code with local repairs (lower surface, higher travel, fewer ironing lines) up to this many times. 0 only reports the hits. Default: 3. Unit: passes. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_road_cooling.label: Curved line cooling
nonplanar_road_cooling.tooltip: Cool and pace each curved line by what it needs. The part and auxiliary fans rise toward the overhang fan speed with the share of the line over nothing and on lines running steeply downhill, early enough to be up when the line arrives. Top surfaces never print faster than the top surface speed, and lines under 2 mm run at the small perimeter speed. With the filament's slowdown for layer cooling on, a curved pass shorter than the minimum layer time slows down and, below the minimum print speed, the nozzle waits above it with the fan at full speed. Printers with rotary axes do not wait. Default: on. Unit: unitless on/off. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_head.label: Print head
nonplanar_head.tooltip: Library ID of the head shape that limits curved surfaces: nozzle, ducts and gantry where modelled. An empty or unknown ID uses the generic conservative head. Default: empty. Unit: head ID or JSON path. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_ignore_duct.label: Ignore cooling duct (experimental)
nonplanar_ignore_duct.tooltip: Leaves the cooling duct out of the print head in every curved slicing method: planning, repair and the collision check see the nozzle, heater block, housing and fans only. Allows steeper curved surfaces; the fan duct may brush the part. Default: off.

nonplanar_head_snapshot.tooltip: Project-owned resolved print-head envelope. Default: empty. Unit: serialized head JSON. Auto retains the saved envelope; changing the head selection clears it.

nonplanar_segment_rate.label: Segment rate
nonplanar_segment_rate.tooltip: How many moves per second the firmware can plan without its move buffer running empty. Curved shells are made of short moves; they are joined and slowed down so that this rate is never exceeded, which avoids stuttering. 0 picks a value from the G-code flavor and printer. Default: 0. Unit: moves/s. Auto retains this setting.

nonplanar_kinematics.label: Rotary axes
nonplanar_kinematics.tooltip: Choose the printer's rotary layout; None keeps ordinary three-axis XYZ motion. Rotary layouts can tilt the tool or bed, but require measured geometry and matching firmware settings. Default: None. Unit: unitless choice. Auto retains this setting.

rotary_axis_limits.label: Rotary axis limits
rotary_axis_limits.tooltip: Allowed firmware angles for the two rotary axes, in order: first minimum, first maximum, second minimum, second maximum. Poses outside these ranges are rejected unless the axis is continuous.

rotary_axis_continuous.label: Continuous rotary axis
rotary_axis_continuous.tooltip: Allow each rotary axis to turn beyond its configured angle limits. Enable only if the hardware, wiring and firmware permit continuous rotation.

rotary_max_speed.label: Rotary axis maximum speed
rotary_max_speed.tooltip: Maximum speed of each rotary axis, used to slow moves and choose rotary motion. Set to 0 to leave that axis without a slicer speed limit.

rotary_pivot.label: Rotary pivot
rotary_pivot.tooltip: X, Y and Z of the rotary axes' intersection in machine coordinates with all linear axes at zero. This point is used to convert nozzle positions into joint moves.

rotary_tool_length.label: Tool length
rotary_tool_length.tooltip: Distance from a tilting head's rotation center to the nozzle tip, or from a rotary table printer's tool mount down to the tip. Used to compensate nozzle motion as the rotary axes turn.

rotary_tool_mount.label: Tool mount
rotary_tool_mount.tooltip: For rotary tables, X, Y and Z of the tool mount in machine coordinates with all linear axes at zero. The nozzle tip sits one tool length below this point.

rotary_table_height.label: Bed height above pivot
rotary_table_height.tooltip: For rotary tables, distance from the rotary pivot to the bed surface along the turntable axis. The work origin is where that axis meets the bed.

rotary_linear_moves_table.label: Linear axis carries the table
rotary_linear_moves_table.tooltip: For rotary tables using joint coordinates, select the X, Y and Z stages that move the table. Their motion has the opposite sign relative to the part from a stage that moves the tool.

rotary_axis_home.label: Rotary axis upright angle
rotary_axis_home.tooltip: Firmware angle of each rotary axis when the tool is upright and the table is unturned. These offsets let ordinary paths print in the machine's upright pose.

rotary_axis_reversed.label: Reverse rotary axis
rotary_axis_reversed.tooltip: Reverse each rotary angle's sign when the firmware's positive direction is opposite to the right-hand rule about that machine axis. The upright angle remains the reference.

rotary_firmware_rtcp.label: Firmware tool center point control
rotary_firmware_rtcp.tooltip: Enable only when the firmware compensates the tool center point for rotary moves (RTCP/TCPC). XYZ then gives the nozzle tip in the work frame and the firmware works out the joint motion.

rotary_inverse_time_feed.label: Inverse time feed (G93)
rotary_inverse_time_feed.tooltip: Write rotary moves with G93 inverse-time feed, where F specifies the reciprocal of the move duration in minutes. Enable only if the controller supports G93; ordinary moves return to G94.

nonplanar_max_tilt.label: Maximum tool tilt
nonplanar_max_tilt.tooltip: Largest angle the tool may lean from the part's vertical on a printer with rotary axes; the rotary axis limits may allow less. Curved top shells lean toward the surface normal only where an upright line would stand proud of the surface, and their bands get shorter so the upright head clears the tilted lines. Other curved areas in height bands stay upright. Multiplanar chunks tilt within this angle; rotary curved layers need at least 10°. 0 keeps the tool upright. On a rotary table, more than 90° lets multiplanar chunks build past horizontal: the table turns a branch that grows sideways or downward until it points up; curved layers still lean at most 90°. Default: 0. Unit: degrees. Auto retains this setting.

layer_change_gcode.label: Layer change G-code
layer_change_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted at every layer change after the Z lift.

silent_mode.label: Silent Mode
silent_mode.tooltip: Whether the machine supports silent mode in which machine uses lower acceleration to print more quietly

emit_machine_limits_to_gcode.label: Emit limits to G-code
emit_machine_limits_to_gcode.tooltip:
If enabled, the machine limits will be emitted to G-code file.
This option will be ignored if the G-code flavor is set to Klipper.

machine_pause_gcode.label: Pause G-code
machine_pause_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the pause print. Users can insert pause G-code in the G-code viewer.

template_custom_gcode.label: Custom G-code
template_custom_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a custom code.

small_area_infill_flow_compensation.label: Small area flow compensation (beta)
small_area_infill_flow_compensation.tooltip: Enable flow compensation for small infill areas.

small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode.label: Flow Compensation Model
small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode.tooltip: Flow Compensation Model, used to adjust the flow for small infill areas. The model is expressed as a comma separated pair of values for extrusion length and flow correction factor. Each pair is on a separate line, followed by a semicolon, in the following format: "1.234, 5.678;"

machine_max_acceleration_x.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the X axis

machine_max_jerk_x.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the X axis

machine_max_acceleration_y.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the Y axis

machine_max_jerk_y.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the Y axis

machine_max_acceleration_z.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the Z axis

machine_max_jerk_z.tooltip: Maximum jerk of the Z axis

machine_max_acceleration_e.tooltip: Maximum acceleration of the E axis

input_shaping_emit.tooltip:

input_shaping_type.label: Input shaper type
input_shaping_type.tooltip:
Choose the input shaper algorithm.

input_shaping_freq_x.tooltip:
Resonant frequency for the X axis input shaper.

input_shaping_freq_y.tooltip:

Damping ratio for the X axis input shaper.

fan_max_speed.label: Fan speed
fan_max_speed.tooltip: The part cooling fan speed may be increased when auto cooling is enabled. This is the maximum speed for the part cooling fan.

max_layer_height.label: Max
max_layer_height.tooltip: The highest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the maximum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.label: Extrusion rate smoothing
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.tooltip:
This parameter smooths out sudden extrusion rate changes that happen when the printer transitions from printing a high flow (high speed/larger width) extrusion to a lower flow (lower speed/smaller width) extrusion and vice versa.

It defines the maximum rate by which the extruded volumetric flow in mm³/s can change over time. Higher values mean higher extrusion rate changes are allowed, resulting in faster speed transitions.

A value of 0 disables the feature.

For a high speed, high flow direct drive printer (like the Bambu lab or Voron) this value is usually not needed. However it can provide some marginal benefit in certain cases where feature speeds vary greatly. For example, when there are aggressive slowdowns due to overhangs. In these cases a high value of around 300-350 mm³/s² is recommended as this allows for just enough smoothing to assist pressure advance achieve a smoother flow transition.

For slower printers without pressure advance, the value should be set much lower. A value of 10-15 mm³/s² is a good starting point for direct drive extruders and 5-10 mm³/s² for Bowden style.

This feature is known as Pressure Equalizer in Prusa slicer.

Note: this parameter disables arc fitting.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.label: Smoothing segment length
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.tooltip:
A lower value results in smoother extrusion rate transitions. However, this results in a significantly larger G-code file and more instructions for the printer to process.

Default value of 3 works well for most cases. If your printer is stuttering, increase this value to reduce the number of adjustments made.

Allowed values: 0.5-5

extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime.label: Apply only on external features
extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime.tooltip: Applies extrusion rate smoothing only on external perimeters and overhangs. This can help reduce artefacts due to sharp speed transitions on externally visible overhangs without impacting the print speed of features that will not be visible to the user.

fan_min_speed.label: Fan speed
fan_min_speed.tooltip: Minimum speed for part cooling fan.

additional_cooling_fan_speed.label: Aux fan speed
additional_cooling_fan_speed.tooltip: Speed for the auxiliary part cooling fan (M106 P2 S0-255) after the initial no-cooling layers. Needs the auxiliary part cooling fan enabled in Printer Settings.

close_additional_fan_first_x_layers.label: For the first
close_additional_fan_first_x_layers.tooltip: Set special auxiliary cooling fan for the first certain layers.

additional_fan_full_speed_layer.label: Full fan speed at layer
additional_fan_full_speed_layer.tooltip: Auxiliary fan speed will be ramped up linearly from layer "For the first" to maximum at layer "Full fan speed at layer". "Full fan speed at layer" will be ignored if lower than "For the first", in which case the fan will run at maximum allowed speed at layer "For the first" + 1.

first_x_layer_fan_speed.label: Fan speed
first_x_layer_fan_speed.tooltip: Special auxiliary cooling fan speed, effective only for the first x layers.

min_layer_height.label: Min
min_layer_height.tooltip: The lowest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the minimum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

slow_down_min_speed.label: Min print speed
slow_down_min_speed.tooltip: The minimum print speed to which the printer slows down to maintain the minimum layer time defined above when the slowdown for better layer cooling is enabled.

notes.label: Configuration notes
notes.tooltip: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.

nozzle_volume.label: Nozzle volume
nozzle_volume.tooltip: Volume of nozzle between the filament cutter and the end of the nozzle

cooling_tube_retraction.label: Cooling tube position
cooling_tube_retraction.tooltip: Distance of the center-point of the cooling tube from the extruder tip.

cooling_tube_length.label: Cooling tube length
cooling_tube_length.tooltip: Length of the cooling tube to limit space for cooling moves inside it.

high_current_on_filament_swap.label: High extruder current on filament swap
high_current_on_filament_swap.tooltip: It may be beneficial to increase the extruder motor current during the filament exchange sequence to allow for rapid ramming feed rates and to overcome resistance when loading a filament with an ugly shaped tip.

parking_pos_retraction.label: Filament parking position
parking_pos_retraction.tooltip: Distance of the extruder tip from the position where the filament is parked when unloaded. This should match the value in printer firmware.

extra_loading_move.label: Extra loading distance
extra_loading_move.tooltip: When set to zero, the distance the filament is moved from parking position during load is exactly the same as it was moved back during unload. When positive, it is loaded further, if negative, the loading move is shorter than unloading.

start_end_points.label: Start end points
start_end_points.tooltip: The start and end points which are from the cutter area to the excess chute.

reduce_infill_retraction.label: Reduce infill retraction
reduce_infill_retraction.tooltip: Don't retract when the travel is entirely within an infill area. That means the oozing can't been seen. This can reduce times of retraction for complex model and save printing time, but make slicing and G-code generating slower. Note that Z-hop is also not performed in areas where retraction is skipped.

ooze_prevention.label: Enable
ooze_prevention.tooltip: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.

filename_format.label: Filename format
filename_format.tooltip: Users can decide project file names when exporting.

make_overhang_printable.label: Make overhangs printable
make_overhang_printable.tooltip: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.

make_overhang_printable_angle.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
make_overhang_printable_angle.tooltip: Maximum angle of overhangs to allow after making more steep overhangs printable.90° will not change the model at all and allow any overhang, while 0 will replace all overhangs with conical material.

make_overhang_printable_hole_size.label: Make overhangs printable - Hole area
make_overhang_printable_hole_size.tooltip: Maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's filled by conical material. A value of 0 will fill all the holes in the model base.

detect_overhang_wall.label: Detect overhang walls
detect_overhang_wall.tooltip: This detects the overhang percentage relative to line width and uses a different speed to print. For 100%% overhang, bridging speed is used.

wave_overhangs.label: Wave overhangs
wave_overhangs.tooltip: Print overhangs too steep for flat layers as rings that grow outward from the supported edge, each anchored to the one before, so 90° ledges print without support. Applies when non-planar mode is not off; where non-planar Auto bends a curved overhang skin under a ledge, that skin prints instead. With supports on, support only fills what the waves leave uncovered.

wave_overhangs_instead_of_bridges.label: Use wave overhangs instead of bridges
wave_overhangs_instead_of_bridges.tooltip: When wave overhangs are enabled, suppress every bridge classification in this region and fill with solid infill instead. Off by default: short, wide flat spans stay as regular bridges; long, concave, one-sided or holed overhangs get waves. Turn on to guarantee no bridge patterns anywhere in the region (bottom bridges and internal bridges both become solid infill).

wave_overhang_outer_perimeters.label: Perimeters
wave_overhang_outer_perimeters.tooltip: Number of outer perimeters preserved inside the overhang region. The rest of the overhang is replaced by the wave pattern. Independent of Quality > Walls: setting this to 1 always gives one outer wall then wave, regardless of how many walls the rest of the object uses. 1 is usually enough. Set to 0 for pure wave (no perimeter at the overhang boundary). Capped at the effective wall count for the layer (e.g. 1 on topmost layers with "only one wall top").

wave_overhang_perimeter_overlap.label: Perimeter overlap
wave_overhang_perimeter_overlap.tooltip: How far (mm) the wave region is grown toward the kept perimeter so the outermost wave line touches the perimeter instead of leaving a gap. Raise it if you see a gap between wave and wall; lower it if wave lines bulge into the wall.

wave_overhang_minimum_width.label: Minimum wave width
wave_overhang_minimum_width.tooltip: Necks in the wave region narrower than this get a thin cut before the waves propagate, so thin fragile branches are not printed. Higher values cut more.

wave_overhang_pattern.label: Pattern
wave_overhang_pattern.tooltip: Controls whether wave-overhang tracks are printed one direction at a time (monotonic), connected into a back-and-forth meander (zig-zag), or started from the better-supported end of each new wave line (smart).

wave_overhang_line_spacing.label: Line spacing
wave_overhang_line_spacing.tooltip: Center-to-center distance between adjacent wave-overhang extrusions.

wave_overhang_flow_mm3_per_mm.label: Wave flow
wave_overhang_flow_mm3_per_mm.tooltip:
Volume of plastic extruded per millimetre of wave-overhang line, in mm³/mm.

Default 0.15 is a calibrated reference value for a 0.4 mm nozzle. The bead hangs in air rather than being squished against a layer below, so layer height has no effect on its cross-section. For non-0.4 mm nozzles, scale as 0.15 × (nozzle/0.4)²: about 0.09 for 0.3 mm, 0.34 for 0.6 mm, 0.60 for 0.8 mm.

Raise if wave lines look thin or broken; lower if they blob together.

wave_overhang_print_speed.label: Print speed
wave_overhang_print_speed.tooltip: Print speed for wave-overhang extrusions. Slow speeds give better cooling and adhesion of the cantilevered tracks. Typical 1 to 5 mm/s. Global setting: object or region overrides are ignored.

wave_overhang_perimeter_speed.label: Perimeter speed
wave_overhang_perimeter_speed.tooltip: Print speed for the walls (perimeters) on layers that contain wave-overhang traces. The walls in those layers anchor onto the cantilevered wave traces, so printing them at the regular outer/inner wall speed often pulls the wave loose or starves adhesion. 0 = inherit the normal wall speed.

wave_overhang_corner_taper_enable.label: Corner reinforcement
wave_overhang_corner_taper_enable.tooltip: When enabled, the wave-overhang generator densifies line spacing near sharp convex corners of the overhang outline. Corners warp worst because their cantilevered wave lines are short and have little neighbouring material to fuse with, so they curl as PLA cools. Packing more lines into a small radius around each corner gives each short line a neighbour to bond with, resisting the curl. The corner line spacing, radius and angle threshold appear when this is on.

wave_overhang_line_spacing_corner.label: Corner line spacing
wave_overhang_line_spacing_corner.tooltip: Line spacing used inside the corner zones. Must be smaller than Line spacing, otherwise corner reinforcement is skipped. About half of Line spacing is a good start.

wave_overhang_corner_taper_distance.label: Corner reinforcement radius
wave_overhang_corner_taper_distance.tooltip: Radius around each detected corner vertex over which the denser spacing is applied. Lines inside this radius use the corner spacing; lines further in use the normal spacing. Larger values widen the reinforced zone at the cost of more extrusion time. Set to 0 to disable corner reinforcement.

wave_overhang_corner_angle_threshold.label: Corner angle threshold
wave_overhang_corner_angle_threshold.tooltip: A vertex on the overhang contour is classified as a corner when its interior angle is smaller than this threshold. Smaller values catch only very sharp corners; larger values flag gentler turns too. 90° is a reasonable default for most shapes.

wave_overhang_floor_layers.label: Floor layers
wave_overhang_floor_layers.tooltip: Number of solid layers forced directly above wave regions to back them up. These layers bridge over the wave surface and give the cantilever mechanical backing. 0 = use only Orca's normal shell settings.

wave_overhang_floor_use_hilbert.label: Hilbert curve floor
wave_overhang_floor_use_hilbert.tooltip: Force the solid floor layers above wave-overhang regions to use a Hilbert curve infill pattern instead of the region's normal solid-infill pattern. Fractal scan paths leave the smallest residual thermal stresses, which significantly reduces warping that pulls long cantilevered overhangs upward as the layers above cool. Opt-in: when off, floor layers retain the existing pattern.

wave_overhang_floor_hilbert_layers.label: Hilbert floor layer count
wave_overhang_floor_hilbert_layers.tooltip: Of the N solid floor layers above each wave region, only the bottom M get the Hilbert pattern; the rest use the default solid-infill pattern. The lowest layers warp most, so capping the Hilbert band saves print time without losing much warping benefit. 0 = match Floor layers (Hilbert on every solid floor).

wave_overhang_floor_hilbert_density.label: Hilbert floor density
wave_overhang_floor_hilbert_density.tooltip: Infill percentage for the Hilbert-pattern floor layers. 100 = recipe-spec solid Hilbert (matches the cited research). Below 100 turns the floor into a sparse Hilbert: faster and less material, at the cost of weaker mechanical backing for the wave below. Experimental setting: 100 is the safe default.

wave_overhang_floor_print_speed.label: Hilbert floor print speed
wave_overhang_floor_print_speed.tooltip: Print speed for the Hilbert-pattern floor layers above wave-overhang regions. Slower speeds give each line more time to dissipate heat before the next neighbouring line lands on top, reducing the residual thermal stress that drives warping. 0 = inherit the normal solid-infill speed.

wave_overhang_floor_perimeter_speed.label: Floor perimeter speed
wave_overhang_floor_perimeter_speed.tooltip: Print speed for the walls (perimeters) on the floor layers above wave-overhang regions. The fragile wave shadow underneath warps when fast walls land on top, so slowing them lets the substrate stay closer to bed temperature and relaxes thermal stress. 0 = inherit the normal wall speed.

wave_overhang_floor_speed_ramp.label: Floor speed ramp
wave_overhang_floor_speed_ramp.tooltip:
Ramps Floor perimeter speed (and Hilbert floor print speed when Hilbert is on) back to normal over this many layers, linearly from the slow override speed up to the normal print/wall speed.

0 = step function: every floor layer prints at the override speed, then snaps back to normal on the next layer.
1..N = layer 1 above the wave prints at the override speed, layer N (or the last floor layer, whichever comes first) prints at full normal speed, with linear interpolation in between.

Helpful for releasing the thermal stress that builds up at the speed transition: the gradual ramp keeps each layer slightly warmer than the next as the print moves away from the wave shadow, so curl is spread across the ramp instead of concentrated at one boundary.

Capped by Floor layers; if you set a ramp longer than the floor-layer count, the ramp ends at the top floor layer.

wave_overhang_min_angle.label: Min angle
wave_overhang_min_angle.tooltip: Not used. Which overhangs get waves is decided by Strength > Detect overhang walls and Overhang reverse threshold. Kept only so older profiles and 3MF files still load.

wave_overhang_spacing_mode.label: Spacing mode
wave_overhang_spacing_mode.tooltip: Reserved, no effect. Ring spacing is always uniform. Kept so older profiles still load.

wave_overhang_seam_mode.label: Seam mode
wave_overhang_seam_mode.tooltip: Reserved, no effect. Ring direction is decided by Pattern. Kept so older profiles still load.

wave_overhang_min_length.label: Min length
wave_overhang_min_length.tooltip: Overhang regions whose outline is shorter than this get no wave and are printed as normal overhangs. Useful to skip tiny overhangs where normal perimeters are fine. 0 = no limit.

wave_overhang_max_iterations.label: Max wave rings
wave_overhang_max_iterations.tooltip: Maximum number of wave rings per overhang region. 0 = unlimited (stops naturally when the waves cannot grow further). Useful for bounding print time on very large overhangs.

wave_overhang_min_new_area.label: Min new area
wave_overhang_min_new_area.tooltip: Termination threshold for wave-overhang propagation: when a new wavefront adds less than this much new area over the previous wavefront, stop propagating. Lower = longer propagation, potentially denser coverage. Higher = earlier termination. Default 0.01 mm² is a safe early-stop; lower toward 0.0001 for maximum coverage.

support_remaining_areas_after_wave_overh.label: Support unfilled wave overhang areas
support_remaining_areas_after_wave_overh.tooltip: When wave overhangs are enabled AND supports are on, only generate supports for overhang areas the wave toolpaths did NOT cover. Explicit support enforcers still apply normally. Disable to let the support generator ignore wave coverage (treats every overhang as if waves weren't there).

unsupported_wall_last.label: Print unsupported walls last
unsupported_wall_last.tooltip:
Wall loops that lie entirely in mid air are printed once something can hold them:
they are extruded after the other walls of their island, innermost first, whatever the wall order is.
A loop that only the bridges of this layer can anchor waits until those bridges are printed, while a loop running alongside a supported wall keeps its place before the infill, which needs it as an anchor.

outer_wall_filament_id.label: Outer walls
outer_wall_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print outer walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

inner_wall_filament_id.label: Inner walls
inner_wall_filament_id.tooltip:
Filament to print inner walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

inner_wall_line_width.label: Inner wall
inner_wall_line_width.tooltip: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

inner_wall_speed.label: Inner wall
inner_wall_speed.tooltip: This is the speed for inner walls.

wall_loops.label: Wall loops
wall_loops.tooltip: This is the number of walls per layer.

alternate_extra_wall.label: Alternate extra wall
alternate_extra_wall.tooltip: Adds an extra inner wall on every other layer so infill locks vertically between the walls for a tougher part. Turn off Ensure vertical shell thickness when using this, and skip it with Lightning infill (which doesn't give the extra wall enough to grab onto).

post_process.label: Post-processing Scripts
post_process.tooltip: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon. Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and they can access the Orca Slicer config settings by reading environment variables.

process_change_extrusion_role_gcode.label: Change extrusion role G-code (process)
process_change_extrusion_role_gcode.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed. It runs after the machine and filament extrusion role G-code.

plugins.label: Plugins Used
plugins.tooltip: Plugin capabilities referenced by this preset, stored as name;uuid;capability.

slicing_pipeline_plugin.label: Slicing Pipeline Plugin
slicing_pipeline_plugin.tooltip: Python plugin(s) invoked at each slicing pipeline step to read and modify intermediate slicing data, including a final G-code post-processing step. Research/experimental.

printer_notes.label: Printer notes
printer_notes.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the printer here.

raft_contact_distance.label: Raft contact Z distance
raft_contact_distance.tooltip: Z gap between raft and object. If Support Top Z Distance is 0, this value is ignored and the object is printed in direct contact with the raft (no gap).

raft_expansion.label: Raft expansion
raft_expansion.tooltip: This expands all raft layers in XY plane.

raft_first_layer_density.label: First layer density
raft_first_layer_density.tooltip: This is the density of the first raft or support layer.

raft_first_layer_expansion.label: First layer expansion
raft_first_layer_expansion.tooltip: This expands the first raft or support layer to improve bed adhesion.

raft_layers.label: Raft layers
raft_layers.tooltip: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when printing ABS.

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.tooltip: The G-code path is generated after simplifying the contour of models to avoid too many points and G-code lines. Smaller values mean higher resolution and more time required to slice.

retraction_minimum_travel.label: Travel distance threshold
retraction_minimum_travel.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

retract_before_wipe.label: Retract amount before wipe
retract_before_wipe.tooltip: This is the length of fast retraction before a wipe, relative to retraction length.

retract_after_wipe.label: Retract amount after wipe
retract_after_wipe.tooltip:
This is the length of fast retraction after wipe, relative to retraction length.
The value will be clamped by 100% minus the retract amount before the wipe value.

retract_when_changing_layer.label: Retract on layer change
retract_when_changing_layer.tooltip: This forces a retraction on layer changes.

retraction_length.label: Length
retraction_length.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

long_retractions_when_cut.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
long_retractions_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

retraction_distances_when_cut.label: Retraction distance when cut
retraction_distances_when_cut.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

retract_length_toolchange.label: Retraction Length (Toolchange)
retract_length_toolchange.tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

z_hop.label: Z-hop height
z_hop.tooltip: Whenever there is a retraction, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. This prevents the nozzle from hitting the print when traveling more. Using spiral lines to lift Z can prevent stringing.

retract_lift_above.label: Only lift Z above
retract_lift_above.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place above the specified absolute Z.

retract_lift_below.label: Only lift Z below
retract_lift_below.tooltip: If you set this to a positive value, Z lift will only take place below the specified absolute Z.

travel_slope.label: Traveling angle
travel_slope.tooltip: Traveling angle for Slope and Spiral Z-hop type. Setting it to 90° results in Normal Lift.

retract_lift_enforce.label: On surfaces
retract_lift_enforce.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

extruder_type.label: Type
extruder_type.tooltip: This setting is only used for initial value of manual calibration of pressure advance. Bowden extruder usually has larger PA value. This setting doesn't influence normal slicing.

default_nozzle_volume_type.label: Default Nozzle Volume Type.
default_nozzle_volume_type.tooltip: Default Nozzle volume type for extruders in this printer.

extruder_nozzle_stats.label: Extruder nozzle stats
extruder_nozzle_stats.tooltip: Physical nozzle counts per extruder, keyed by nozzle volume type.

extruder_nozzle_volume_type.label: Extruder nozzle volume type
extruder_nozzle_volume_type.tooltip: Nozzle volume type per physical nozzle of an extruder.

enable_filament_dynamic_map.label: Enable filament dynamic map
enable_filament_dynamic_map.tooltip: Enable dynamic filament mapping during print.

has_filament_switcher.label: Has filament switcher
has_filament_switcher.tooltip: Printer has a filament switcher hardware (e.g., AMS).

master_extruder_id.label: Master extruder id
master_extruder_id.tooltip: Default extruder id to place filament.

retract_restart_extra.label: Extra length on restart
retract_restart_extra.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

retract_restart_extra_toolchange.label: Extra length on restart (Toolchange)
retract_restart_extra_toolchange.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

retraction_speed.label: Retraction speed
retraction_speed.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

deretraction_speed.label: Deretraction speed
deretraction_speed.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

deretract_speed_extruder_change.label: Deretraction speed (extruder change)
deretract_speed_extruder_change.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle when switching extruder.

use_firmware_retraction.label: Use firmware retraction
use_firmware_retraction.tooltip: This experimental setting uses G10 and G11 commands to have the firmware handle the retraction. This is only supported in recent Marlin.

disable_m73.label: Disable set remaining print time
disable_m73.tooltip: Disable generating of the M73: Set remaining print time in the final G-code.

seam_position.label: Seam position
seam_position.tooltip: This is the starting position for each part of the outer wall.

staggered_inner_seams.label: Staggered inner seams
staggered_inner_seams.tooltip: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

seam_gap.label: Seam gap
seam_gap.tooltip:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current extruder diameter. The default value for this parameter is 10%.

seam_slope_type.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)
seam_slope_type.tooltip: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.

seam_slope_conditional.label: Conditional scarf joint
seam_slope_conditional.tooltip: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.

scarf_angle_threshold.label: Conditional angle threshold
scarf_angle_threshold.tooltip:
This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam.
If the maximum angle within the perimeter loop exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.

scarf_overhang_threshold.label: Conditional overhang threshold
scarf_overhang_threshold.tooltip: This option determines the overhang threshold for the application of scarf joint seams. If the unsupported portion of the perimeter is less than this threshold, scarf joint seams will be applied. The default threshold is set at 40% of the external wall's width. Due to performance considerations, the degree of overhang is estimated.

scarf_joint_speed.label: Scarf joint speed
scarf_joint_speed.tooltip: This option sets the printing speed for scarf joints. It is recommended to print scarf joints at a slow speed (less than 100 mm/s). It's also advisable to enable 'Extrusion rate smoothing' if the set speed varies significantly from the speed of the outer or inner walls. If the speed specified here is higher than the speed of the outer or inner walls, the printer will default to the slower of the two speeds. When specified as a percentage (e.g., 80%), the speed is calculated based on the respective outer or inner wall speed. The default value is set to 100%.

scarf_joint_flow_ratio.label: Scarf joint flow ratio
scarf_joint_flow_ratio.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of material for scarf joints.

seam_slope_start_height.label: Scarf start height
seam_slope_start_height.tooltip:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.

seam_slope_entire_loop.label: Scarf around entire wall
seam_slope_entire_loop.tooltip: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.

seam_slope_min_length.label: Scarf length
seam_slope_min_length.tooltip: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.

seam_slope_steps.label: Scarf steps
seam_slope_steps.tooltip: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.

seam_slope_inner_walls.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
seam_slope_inner_walls.tooltip: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.

role_based_wipe_speed.label: Role base wipe speed
role_based_wipe_speed.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed of the current extrusion role. e.g. if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.

wipe_on_loops.label: Wipe on loops
wipe_on_loops.tooltip: To minimize the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, a small inward movement is executed before the extruder leaves the loop.

wipe_inward.label: Wipe inward
wipe_inward.tooltip:
Applies only to external walls, including hole boundaries. Moves the hot nozzle toward printed inner walls during wiping to reduce reheating of freshly printed plastic and seam marks.

Especially useful at layer heights below 0.1 mm, where wipe marks are more visible.

Uses the regular wipe if no adjacent inner wall is already printed (single-wall areas or Outer/Inner wall order), or if no supported inward path can be found, for example at tight corners or seam gaps.

wipe_inward_distance.label: Wipe inward distance
wipe_inward_distance.tooltip:
The distance the wipe path is shifted away from the external perimeter, specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the actual outer-wall extrusion width.

For example, 50% shifts the path by half of the outer-wall width. The effective offset is limited by both the actual outer-wall width and the available spacing to the adjacent wall, so values above 100% or an equivalent absolute distance have no additional effect. Set to 0 to disable the offset.

wipe_before_external_loop.label: Wipe before external loop
wipe_before_external_loop.tooltip:
To minimize visibility of potential overextrusion at the start of an external perimeter when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order, the de-retraction is performed slightly on the inside from the start of the external perimeter. That way any potential over extrusion is hidden from the outside surface.
